At the IBC conference, running Sept. 11-14 in Amsterdam, the creative, technology and business communities are coming together to turn ideas into action and discuss innovations across the media and entertainment industries. More than 44,000 attendees from 170+ countries are gathering to explore 1,300+ exhibitions in 14+ halls and outdoor spaces, with over 600 speakers delivering insights.

Read on to learn more about what NVIDIA’s highlighting at the show.

NVIDIA AI for Media Brings Real-Time Intelligence to Broadcast, Sports and Production Workflows

Media companies are increasingly integrating AI into live production, sports, news and streaming workflows to unlock richer performance insights, verify video authenticity, and enhance and localize content — all without disrupting trusted broadcast environments.

At IBC 2026 in Amsterdam, NVIDIA announced a major expansion to NVIDIA AI for Media — a collection of GPU-accelerated software development kits (SDKs), NVIDIA NIM microservices, playbooks, and blueprints that enhance audio, video and augmented-reality effects for media and entertainment workflows — to unlock new ways to understand motion, verify and enhance video, localize programming and build AI-powered media applications. 

The NVIDIA Synthetic Video Detector (SVD) NIM microservice, announced earlier this year at SIGGRAPH, helps organizations assess the probability of whether footage is authentic or AI-generated, giving editorial, content-authentication, digital-forensics and media-integrity teams another point of analysis in their review process.

Since its initial release, SVD’s accuracy has reached 99.3% for text-to-video content and 97.7% for image-to-video content, with especially large gains on difficult image-to-video cases. 

Dalet is integrating SVD into a secure, cloud-hosted verification workflow for news organizations. This allows editorial teams to submit footage through SVD, inspect and review the resulting scores and metadata within a Dalet interface. 

TwelveLabs announced the general availability of Compliance by TwelveLabs, its first application built on the company’s video intelligence platform, helping media and broadcast teams rapidly screen content against regional and custom compliance standards. The solution integrates SVD to add frame-level authenticity signals and confidence scores, enabling media teams to identify potentially synthetic media within the same compliance workflow.

Wowza, whose Wowza Streaming Engine media server technology powers more than 35,000 video deployments across over 170 countries, will distribute SVD through the Wowza Video Intelligence Framework. The solution, powered by NVIDIA-accelerated infrastructure, will enable broadcasters, streaming providers and other organizations to analyze live video feeds and extract data around detected objects, scenes and signs of AI generation in real time. It can be deployed and run on premises, at the edge, in the cloud, across hybrid deployments or fully air-gapped, giving organizations greater control over critical media workflows.

NVIDIA 3D Body Pose estimates 2D and 3D human joint locations and angles from video captured by a single camera, helping turn motion into structured data without marker-based capture systems.

For sports organizations, that data can support player and athlete movement tracking, biomechanics and performance analysis, replay enhancement, officiating and adjudication workflows, player-safety applications, and virtual interaction and immersive experiences. 

The technology can also provide structured human-motion data for content-creation workflows. When mapped to a compatible character rig, joint and motion data can serve as input for animation blocking, digital doubles, character retargeting and virtual-production experiences.

Vizrt is using Body Pose technology in live virtual-studio environments, with tracked body movement driving real-time 3D lighting effects such as reflections, shadows and environmental rendering.

Video Frame Generation (VFG) makes video motion appear smoother by using generative AI to create new frames between the original frames of a video. It can increase frame rates by 2x or 4x while preserving visual quality and temporal consistency, enabling more fluid sports, slow-motion replays, live media and other high-motion video experiences. VFG also supports frame-rate conversion and frame boosting for generative AI video workflows.

Ross Video is integrating VFG into its Rio Replay platform to create AI-assisted slow-motion video for sports production.

The work supports 6x slow-motion generation for sports replay. Development is underway toward 8x interpolation, meaning generated intermediate frames can give replay teams smoother motion without requiring every frame to be captured by an ultrahigh-frame-rate source camera. 

NVIDIA Video Super Resolution (VSR) uses AI to upscale video while reducing noise, blur and compression artifacts. New streaming modes let developers choose between real-time performance and higher image quality, while adjustable controls help achieve the desired level of enhancement. VSR also adds 10-bit video support and improves overall performance and quality. VSR is available through the NVIDIA Video Effects SDK and a NIM microservice for use in streaming, broadcast, conferencing, video playback and content-creation applications. 

The technology can support video players, conferencing applications, creator tools, streaming services, transcoders and broadcast systems through a common interface.

NVIDIA TrueHDR converts standard-dynamic-range video into high-dynamic-range output in real time, reaching up to approximately 2,000 nits while preserving local contrast and adapting brightness to the content.

VSR, VFG and TrueHDR can be combined within a single video-effects pipeline — helping media companies enhance existing content libraries for streaming, transcoding, gaming and creator workflows.  

The NVIDIA LipSync and Active Speaker Detection NIM microservices help developers build localization systems for interviews, news, sports, entertainment and other programming where multiple people may appear on screen.

LipSync transforms mouth movement in an input video to match a target audio track while preserving natural head pose, blinking and body movement. The new release improves facial occlusion handling and better preserves teeth, lip and facial textures.

The new Active Speaker Detection NIM microservice no longer requires speaker diarization for multiple audio tracks, adds voice activity detection and expands NIM microservice deployment support through a gRPC interface and broader GPU compatibility.

NDI is using NVIDIA AI for Media, including the NVIDIA LipSync NIM microservice, to enable real-time translation, lip-synced dubbing and regional language adaptation within existing broadcast workflows. By generating multiple language experiences from a common media stream, the approach can help broadcasters reach global audiences while reducing the bandwidth, infrastructure and production complexity traditionally required for multilingual distribution.

Studio Voice includes new Microphone Profiles built on NVIDIA Studio Voice NIM microservices, giving users more control over the tonal character of enhanced speech.

The capability is designed to suppress background noise, reduce room reverberation and improve speech clarity, then shape the enhanced output into a selected microphone profile for more polished live communications, streaming, podcasting and content creation.

Try NVIDIA AI for Media NIM microservices. See the latest NVIDIA and partner workflows at IBC 2026.

NVIDIA Holoscan for Media Provides Open Media Exchange Layer to Build and Connect Live Media Applications

As broadcasters, streaming services and sports organizations adopt software and AI, the infrastructure behind live content is becoming more flexible, more connected and increasingly built on shared accelerated computing.

The integration of Media Exchange Layer (MXL) with NVIDIA Holoscan for Media accelerates that transition — providing the common exchange layer that helps media applications connect and operate together. 

Holoscan for Media is an open reference architecture and developer toolkit for building AI-powered media functions and applications for software-defined live production. MXL adds an open way for those software-based media functions to exchange live video, audio and data across a distributed environment. 

As production functions move into software, developers can build applications that share accelerated infrastructure, connect dynamically and evolve independently. That can help media companies use infrastructure more efficiently, introduce new capabilities faster and reduce the amount of custom integration required between applications.

The integration also creates a stronger foundation for AI in live media. AI processing, video applications and traditional media functions can increasingly operate on the same accelerated infrastructure and in the same software-defined environment.

For technology vendors, this expands the opportunity to build applications that can work across broader, multi-vendor ecosystems. For media companies, it creates a path toward infrastructure that can adapt as formats, applications and AI capabilities change.

See the demo at IBC in EBU Stand 10.D21. ​Learn more about Holoscan for Media.

NVIDIA Sports Intelligence Playbooks Chart a Path to Multimodal AI for Sports

Sports is becoming a proving ground for a broader shift in AI: from general-purpose models toward fine-tuned open models built on proprietary data.

NVIDIA Sports Intelligence Playbooks are designed to accelerate that transition. They give leagues, media companies and technology providers structured frameworks to fine-tune NVIDIA open models on their own sports footage and annotations, creating multimodal AI that can understand the rules, players, scoring, strategy and context unique to a sport.

Sports organizations hold large volumes of proprietary video, metadata and performance information that are difficult for competitors to replicate. The playbooks provide a practical blueprint for converting those assets into AI capabilities that can underpin new analytics products, media experiences, automation tools and revenue streams.

The playbooks span the AI lifecycle, including data preparation, fine-tuning, inference, evaluation, optimization and deployment, and bring together NVIDIA technologies including Nemotron, NeMo AutoModel, Megatron Bridge, NIM microservices and NVIDIA accelerated computing. 

By providing an integrated path from model customization to production, Sports Intelligence Playbooks can reduce the cost and complexity of building specialized sports AI while increasing demand across its compute, software and inference stack.

Early testing demonstrates the potential of domain specialization. When evaluated on previously unseen footage using question formats similar to those used in training,  multiple-choice accuracy increased from approximately 53% to 94% and open-ended evaluation from approximately 5.7% to 66%.

Machina Sports is integrating Sports Intelligence Playbooks with its sports-native data, evaluation and agent infrastructure, enabling rights holders to turn proprietary media and expertise into private, deployable intelligence for live production, content and fan experiences.

The opportunity also expands as agentic AI becomes increasingly adopted. With the NVIDIA AI-Q Blueprint, organizations can use their domain-specific sports models as expert intelligence within agents that reason across video, enterprise data and software systems, extending the playbook from sports understanding into decision-making and automation.

Wowza is integrating vision language models, including NVIDIA Cosmos 3 and Nemotron, into the Wowza Video Intelligence Framework, fine-tuned through NVIDIA Sports Intelligence Playbooks to detect sports-specific moments in live streams and reduce time to action. 

Explore NVIDIA Sports Intelligence Playbooks.

NVIDIA Brings Multilingual Content Localization to Live Broadcast

Reaching global audiences with live programming requires more than translating words. Language nuances, voice, timing, facial movement, captions and onscreen graphics must work together in real time, while preserving the editorial intent and production quality of the original program.

Content Localization with Holoscan for Media incorporates the latest advancements from NVIDIA AI for Media, including improved LipSync when faces are partially obscured and enhanced Active Speaker Detection to help applications identify who’s speaking in multi-person scenes.

Expanding the Reach of Live Programming

Localization can transform the reach and economics of live programming. A shared, composable workflow can help media companies introduce regional coverage faster, serve more audiences and tailor experiences for individual markets — while preserving the timing, visual context and editorial control required for live production.

Technologies from AI-Media, CAMB.AI, Chyron and Panjaya each address a specific part of content localization with Holoscan for Media, from adapting voice and onscreen delivery to creating multilingual captions and translated audio, localizing graphics, and preserving expression and identity across live and on-demand content.

The Content Localization technologies also support file-based, streaming and post-production applications. Developers can use application programming interfaces for on-demand workflows and the Holoscan for Media reference workflow when localization must run as part of a live media environment. Together, they provide a consistent foundation for building multilingual media services across production and distribution.

Learn more about NVIDIA Holoscan for Media and AI for Media.

title: Sparks Fly: NVIDIA Accelerates Local AI at IFA 2026
text: Frontier intelligence is going local. At IFA 2026, NVIDIA, Microsoft and its partners are teaming up to provide faster inference and new tools that make agents easier to set up and run locally on NVIDIA hardware. New compact NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows PCs are also coming in October to give AI enthusiasts, developers and creators more ways to run capable agents locally and securely. Today’s announcements include: Simplified local AI support for NVIDIA GPUs is coming in Hermes Agent, OpenClaw and Perplexity Portable Computer. Up to 1.9x faster local inference — new llama.cpp and vLLM optimizations are available now directly and through LM Studio and Ollama. NVIDIA PAIR — a Personal AI Router tool that intelligently distributes AI inference across the PCs on a user’s local network. NVIDIA RTX Spark arrives in October — with new Windows PCs from Lenovo and Acer. Electronic Arts, Embark and Ubisoft are among the latest game publishers and developers bringing their blockbuster titles to NVIDIA RTX Spark. Also, August was a busy month for local AI : Nemotron 3.5 Lightning — which can run on NVIDIA RTX PCs, RTX PRO Workstations, DGX Spark and Jetson — is a 30-billion parameter model that has been launched. Get started with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning today. Z.ai’s GLM-5.3-Flash is a multimodal mixture-of-experts (MoE) model that’s bringing agentic AI to DGX Station. Qwen has released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next , an open weight multimodal MoE model, which can run locally on DGX Spark and DGX Station, along with Qwen3.8-27B , a 27-billion-parameter open model optimized for local agentic and coding workloads on NVIDIA GPUs. LTX’s LTX 2.5 is an open-world video generation model optimized for NVIDIA RTX GPUs, DGX Spark and DGX Station, with new NVFP4, FastVideo and ComfyUI enhancements for faster, more memory-efficient local generation. MiniMax-H3 is an open-weight video generation model with synchronized audio that can run locally on NVIDIA GPUs through ComfyUI. FastVideo teamed up with NVIDIA researchers to improve this further by releasing FastH3 — an open-weight, four-step distilled version that improves performance by 7x. Optimized FastVideo recipes for NVIDIA RTX GPUs and DGX Spark are coming soon. Meta’s Muse Glimmer is a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model for coding and agentic workloads that can run locally on GeForce RTX PCs, DGX Spark, DGX Station and Jetson. NVIDIA has also released NVFP4 quantization with DGX Spark support for more memory-efficient local deployment. DeepSeek v4 Flash is a 284-billion-parameter MoE model with 13 billion active parameters that can run locally on 2x DGX Spark cluster and DGX Station. A Simpler Start for Local Agents Getting a local agent up and running with local models required some effort — choosing a model, finding a compatible inference server, dialing in quantization settings and keeping everything updated. That friction is disappearing on RTX and DGX systems. Three of the most widely used agent apps will offer simplified local model setup on Windows, each built on llama.cpp and incorporating NVIDIA’s latest inference optimizations. The new setup experiences are designed to reduce manual configuration and make it easier to get local agents up and running. Last month, Perplexity introduced its Portable Computer agent , giving users a simple way to run Perplexity locally on Linux systems like NVIDIA DGX Spark with the models, orchestration and tools packaged into a single app experience. Perplexity Portable Computer is available on NVIDIA RTX GPUs with at least 24GB VRAM running on Linux, with support on Windows coming soon, bringing that same streamlined setup to a broader group of PC users. Users can run complete workflows locally without consuming credits, while selectively escalating parts of a task to one of 15+ frontier models in the cloud when additional research or reasoning is needed. Portable Computer asks for permission before sending content to the cloud, helping users keep sensitive information on their device. Here’s some example use-cases: Engineering: Review open PRs in a connected GitHub repo and sort them into ready, blocked, stale, and needs review, each tagged with the next step. Docs that fell out of sync with the latest merge get caught and fixed, with a PR opened for the changes. Finance: Point the agent at two years of brokerage summaries, consolidated 1099s and tax returns and have it trace the recurring holdings creating the most avoidable fees and tax drag, with every figure cited to the exact file and page — all without a document ever reaching a chatbot. Startups: Ask why activation went flat, and the agent analyzes the funnel export locally to find where new signups drop off between install and first completed task, then posts the top insights straight to the team’s Slack channel. Try Portable Computer today. Hermes Agent — developed by Nous Research — is a general-purpose agent used by millions that excels at reliability and self-improvement. Model- and provider-agnostic, Hermes is built to run all day on local systems, making RTX PCs, RTX PRO workstations and DGX Spark a natural fit. Configuring a local model in Hermes will provide users with one-click setup across RTX and DGX systems on Windows. The agent will automatically detect the NVIDIA GPU, select an appropriate model and configuration, and run it through integrated llama.cpp with NVIDIA inference optimizations already in place, eliminating manual model downloads and tuning. Support for Linux is coming soon. Once it is running, Hermes works the way it does anywhere else. It uses tools, maintains context across tasks, remembers information between sessions and creates reusable skills over time, allowing the agent to become more capable with continued use. Running the model locally on a GPU keeps performance fast while keeping data on the system. One-click local model setup is available now on Windows, with support coming soon to Linux. Learn more about Hermes Agent . OpenClaw has become one of the defining projects of the open-agent movement — the largest AI project on GitHub, with more than 380K stars and a fast-growing community that’s building tools and skills across research, engineering, project management and everyday productivity. NVIDIA, Microsoft and OpenClaw have been working together to make that experience easier to set up on Windows PCs. To reduce onboarding friction, the OpenClaw Windows App simplifies the process of setting up an optimized local model on any RTX GPU with at least 24GB of VRAM. Learn more in the OpenClaw blog . Faster Inference Gives Local Agents a Boost Inference performance is critical to keeping local agents responsive. NVIDIA is continuing to collaborate with the open-source llama.cpp and vLLM communities to accelerate agentic workloads across local NVIDIA platforms. llama.cpp delivers up to 1.9x higher throughput through kernel optimizations on a GeForce RTX 5090, enhanced speculative decoding techniques and faster prefill. ​ vLLM delivers 1.2x on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition and up to 1.4x on two DGX Spark clusters. New XQA attention kernels in FlashInfer and backend optimizations help to accelerate inference across both platforms. These gains are available on the llama.cpp and vLLM inferencing backends. Users can also experience these via the LM Studio and Ollama applications. Tap Idle PCs for More Local AI Compute With NVIDIA PAIR More than half of U.S. households have two or more PCs, and much of that computing power sits idle throughout the day. NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR) is a free, open source software tool that puts those systems to work together for local AI. Agentic workflows often break complex tasks into smaller jobs that can run in parallel, but performance can slow when every request is competing for the same GPU. PAIR automatically discovers compatible PCs on a local network and routes independent inference requests to whichever system has capacity. It works with Ollama and LM Studio and can adapt as devices join or leave the network. For example, a user could ask Hermes to create a “Sunday Reset” plan by sorting through a cluttered inbox and prioritizing what needs attention now, what can wait and what can be skipped. Hermes can split that work across multiple subagents, while PAIR distributes those jobs across available PCs instead of having them all wait on a single GPU. The result is more compute for local agents, with more tasks running in parallel and the flexibility to move AI workloads to another PC while the main system is being used for gaming, creating or other work. The NVIDIA PAIR beta is available for Windows, macOS and Linux through both graphical and terminal interfaces, supporting NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20 Series GPUs and newer, NVIDIA RTX PRO workstation GPUs (Turing architecture and newer), NVIDIA DGX Spark and Apple M4 or newer silicon. Check out the NVIDIA tech blog to get started with NVIDIA PAIR. Powerful On Device Photo Editing With Cyberlink PhotoDirector AI PC Mode on RTX Spark Open image and video models enable artists to experiment with Creative AI models on PCs. This enables artists to iterate and explore concepts and ideas, without the dreaded token anxiety and keep more of their creative work private and on-device. CyberLink’s new PhotoDirector AI PC Mode is one of the first applications to integrate these diffusion models directly into a creative software, and turn them into a creative tool at the finger tips of the artists. Coming to PhotoDirector 365 and optimized for NVIDIA RTX Spark when it launches, AI PC Mode users are getting AI-powered editing tools for generative editing, image enhancement, object and distraction removal, background removal and replacement, portrait refinement and the creation of entirely new visuals — with the flexibility to choose between local or cloud processing, depending on the task. On NVIDIA GPUs, PhotoDirector uses TensorRT-RTX and FP8 to accelerate local AI. Start using Cyberlink’s PhotoDirector 365 photo editing software and learn more about PhotoDirector AI PC Mode, launching with RTX Spark in October. NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows PCs Arrive October 2026 NVIDIA RTX Spark is coming this October— and at IFA 2026, partners are showing off their hardware. At IFA, newly announced designs join the existing six OEMs shipping in October. Acer showed its compact desktop RTX Spark concept, and Lenovo announced its Yoga Pro 9n and Yoga 9n 2-in-1. RTX Spark is a new beginning for Windows PCs. One PC built for creators, gamers and AI agents. With a powerful 1 Petaflop RTX Blackwell GPU, up to 128GB of unified memory and a highly efficient 20-core Grace CPU, RTX Spark delivers incredible performance and efficiency. This superchip enables high performance thin laptops with all day battery life and compact desktops to power always-on agents. Paired with the new Windows Agent framework, it enables agents that run safely in the background under OS level control. Last week at Gamescom, Electronic Arts, Embark and Ubisoft were among the latest game publishers and developers bringing their blockbuster titles to NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows PCs. They join the publishers that announced RTX Spark support at COMPUTEX in May, including KRAFTON, NetEase, Riot Games and XBOX. Read more . Sign up to be notified when RTX Spark laptops and desktops are available. #ICYMI: More Updates From NVIDIA Local AI NVIDIA Brings New RTX Tech and Games to Gamescom — NVIDIA released DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction , featuring a new second-generation transformer model for improved image quality in ray-traced and path-traced games. Gamescom also brought new RTX announcements for titles including 007 First Light, CONTROL Resonant and Gears of War: E-Day, plus expanded game support for the upcoming NVIDIA RTX Spark. Introducing DeepSeek Harness — DeepSeek’s new open source harness pairs with DeepSeek-V4-Flash to power local agentic coding workflows on NVIDIA DGX Station and multi-DGX Spark setups. MLPerf Client v2.0 Expands AI PC Benchmarking — MLCommons released MLPerf Client v2.0 , developed in collaboration with NVIDIA and other industry leaders. The update adds new benchmarks for agentic AI and image generation, alongside expanded LLM testing for real-world local AI workloads. Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X , Instagram , TikTok and Facebook — and stay informed by subscribing to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter . Follow NVIDIA Workstation on LinkedIn and X . See notice regarding software product information.

title: From AI ambition to business impact
text: Most business leaders I meet no longer need to be convinced that AI works. They’ve seen the pilots, the demos and the copilots. The question I hear in boardrooms now is different: How do we move from AI that impresses to AI that changes how the business actually runs? That is the question Microsoft Frontier Company was built to answer, and to date, we have engaged on nearly 500 projects with over 200 customers across 28 countries. Customers including 3M, Alaska Airlines, BMW, Core42, KT, Land O’Lakes, London Stock Exchange Group, Mastercard, McKesson, Northern Trust, Novo Nordisk, Publicis Groupe, Saint-Gobain, Siemens and Unilever are seeing real value from working side by side with our Forward Deployed Engineering teams. More importantly, most customers where we have completed initial projects have returned for additional engagements, generating hundreds of follow-on projects. Customers don’t come back for engineers. They come back because the first engagement delivered something they could measure and they can see the next workflow worth redesigning. The technology is ready. What slows AI down is everything around it. That means identifying where AI can deliver the greatest value, building in trust and governance, redesigning the operating models and helping people work in new ways. Technology and people have to move forward together. What this looks like in practice Unilever is collaborating with Microsoft engineers to bring AI into its factories. On the factory floor, intelligent technology helps teams boost efficiency and deliver superior products to customers. In Pondicherry factory — Unilever’s largest Home Care Liquids factory in South Asia and a 2026 World Economic Forum Lighthouse site — a digital twin built on NVIDIA Omniverse and hosted on Azure simulates a real factory environment with integrated live data. This helps anticipate issues before they occur, monitors performance in real time and guides operators through the fixes and recommendations. 3M is working with our engineers to help its Global Business Services team automate customer order management. The companies are building an AI agent-driven workflow to assist with credit checks, delinquency assessments and system updates, with human-in-the-loop controls and a custom monitoring dashboard for real-time visibility and approvals. The solution is expected to significantly reduce manual effort, improve speed and consistency and accelerate cash flow — freeing staff for higher-value work while enabling scalable, auditable operations. Publicis Groupe is co-building with our engineers to bring AI into the heart of how it works and delivers for clients. Microsoft engineers work side by side with Publicis teams to design and build agentic processes grounded in Microsoft IQ, so agents work with the business context, data and knowledge behind Publicis’ work. These processes use reinforcement learning, drawing on real-world outcomes and human feedback to keep improving how the agents perform over time. The approach combines very fast engineering with hands-on knowledge transfer, helping Publicis build lasting AI capability. The work builds on Publicis’ rollout of Microsoft 365 Copilot to all 114,000 of its employees. Northern Trust needed to accelerate onboarding to its Asset Servicing Front Office Solutions platform, a process that took about two and a half weeks per client. Our engineers worked alongside Northern Trust’s experts to build an AI-powered onboarding agent within the Excel and SharePoint tools analysts already use. The result: data preparation time fell 83%, from two and a half weeks to three days, with 96.5% first pass quality score in testing . Analysts remain in control while gaining more time for higher-value client service. KT , one of South Korea’s largest telecommunications providers, wanted to help network operators identify and respond to problems faster. Our engineers worked from KT’s offices to co-build AIO-Net, a continuously learning AI agent platform informed by KT’s operating procedures and veteran network experts. It now detects network issues in two to three minutes, down from more than ten, while keeping people in control of decisions and actions. Saint-Gobain , the 360-year-old construction materials company, is using AI to help reduce the carbon footprint of cement. Working alongside its researchers, Microsoft engineers used Microsoft Discovery to gather 62,000 patents and 44,000 research abstracts into a knowledge base in hours, work Saint-Gobain estimates would have taken researchers a year. In about six weeks, the team identified new hypotheses for cement additives that scientists are now testing in the lab. Across all of these customers, the pattern is the same: Begin with the value , not the technology. Redesign the process , not just the task. Build in fast cycles with the customer’s teams. Put security, governance and cost management in place from day one , so scaling doesn’t stall. This is how organizations move from isolated AI projects to sustainable transformation: by focusing on measurable outcomes, redesigning work and building the capabilities to keep improving over time. New research from IDC underscores why this approach matters. While 66% of organizations report substantial or transformative results from AI, only 48% are scaling or seeing consistent value across their organizations. At the same time, 71% expect AI spending to increase by at least 10% in the next year, putting even greater pressure on businesses to demonstrate measurable returns. The challenge is no longer simply adopting AI. It is reimagining how work gets done and turning that transformation into lasting business impact. We’re holding ourselves to the same standard If we’re asking customers to redesign how they work around AI, we have to do the same. Microsoft Frontier Company was deliberately designed to be flat and fast, with one front door for customers, and as a reference for what an AI-native organization can look like. We are learning, adjusting and moving fast, the same way we ask our customers to. The real measure of success The gap between AI that impresses and AI that delivers won’t close on its own. It closes workflow by workflow, with people who understand the business sitting next to people who can build. Our success will be measured by more than what we deliver. The real test is what our customers can do after we’ve worked together: run, govern and improve their own AI systems, on their terms, with their intelligence protected. Their success is the clearest measure of ours. Learn more at www.microsoft.com/en-us/frontier-company . Rodrigo Kede Lima is the President of Microsoft Frontier Company and leads the operating business of 6,000 industry and engineering experts focused on delivering Frontier Transformation through AI for customers around the world. title: Scaling AI value without losing control: Lessons from Frontier Firms
text: Results are widespread. Value at scale is not, and that gap is what this year’s research from IDC , commissioned by Microsoft, set out to explain. In our fourth year commissioning IDC, more than 5,200 senior IT and business leaders across 28 industries shared what it takes to maximize value as AI scales. The clearest lessons come from Frontier Firms, the group last year’s research introduced: the top 10% of organizations on IDC’s AI maturity scale. What the research found Frontier Firms lead on return. They report an average 4x return on AI versus 2.7x for slow adopters (the bottom 30% on IDC’s scale), and 39% see returns of 5x or more versus 4% of slow adopters. Measurement is the next test . Only 61% of organizations are highly confident they can measure AI’s business value and ROI, versus 93% of Frontier Firms. Governance is in place, but confidence lags. 65% of organizations have an established process to govern agents, yet only 60% have high confidence in addressing AI security and governance risks. Workforce readiness is uneven. 67% say their workforce reports high trust in AI, yet only 20% have a comprehensive, organization-wide skilling strategy. “Organizations that scale AI value aren’t simply spending more. They manage AI investments, models, agents, governance and skills as one discipline, and that is what turns early results into value they can repeat across the business,” says Kathy Lange, Research Director, AI, Data and Automation Software, IDC. AI value now reaches well beyond cost savings Organizations now use AI in 6.5 business areas on average, led by IT infrastructure, cybersecurity and customer service, with the fastest growth in industry-specific uses. Employee experience, revenue growth, customer experience, innovation and risk reduction now rank nearly even as the places AI strengthens the business. Cost is an important consideration, but it is evaluated alongside accuracy, security, compliance and scalability. Where scale stalls 66% of leaders say AI has delivered substantial or transformative results, but only 48% are scaling that value across multiple business units. Agents follow the same pattern: 36% of organizations are still piloting them. The widest gap is people: workforce confidence is running well ahead of the plans to support it. The organizations pulling ahead are closing these gaps by design. Inside the Frontier Firm IDC’s maturity scale weighs spending discipline, breadth of use, agent adoption, skills, confidence in managing AI risk and outcomes. On agents specifically, Frontier Firms report a 3.8x return versus 3.0x for slow adopters. These returns are leader-reported, and the research shows association rather than cause. What they do differently comes down to five behaviors: They invest ahead of plan . 90% of Frontier Firms exceeded their planned AI spend. They deploy AI broadly , across most of the business, not just a few teams. They put agents to work . 96% are rolling out agents at scale, and 53% orchestrate them across workflows. They govern so they can scale . 87% have a process to govern and oversee agents, versus 51% of slow adopters. They build skills everywhere . 80% have an organization-wide AI skilling strategy, versus 3% of slow adopters. At Bristol Myers Squibb , the RABIT agent “connects the dots across meetings, helping teams make better decisions while reducing administrative follow-up work,” says Lakshman Yerramalla, Director of Portfolio Governance and Delivery for Global Manufacturing Operations. Project managers who use it save up to an estimated 20% of their time. Four disciplines for scaling AI value The lesson from Frontier Firms is one I believe every leader can act on: scaling AI value means managing models, agents, governance and measurement as one accountable system. Value and control aren’t a trade-off. I see the same pattern with customers: the organizations scaling fastest treat AI as a change in how the business runs, not a technology rollout. “The skilling that a lot of companies miss is the business skilling,” says Eric Tabor, Chief Digital Officer, KOHLER . “We also focus on how to dissect processes and convert them into AI workflows.” Unlock model choice Trust and security, leading-edge technology and model performance tie as the top criteria for choosing an AI platform (44% each). Results are widespread. Value at scale is not, and that gap is what this year’s research from IDC, commissioned by Microsoft, set out to explain.

In our fourth year commissioning IDC, more than 5,200 senior IT and business leaders across 28 industries shared what it takes to maximize value as AI scales. The clearest lessons come from Frontier Firms, the group last year’s research introduced: the top 10% of organizations on IDC’s AI maturity scale.

What the research found 

  • Frontier Firms lead on return. They report an average 4x return on AI versus 2.7x for slow adopters (the bottom 30% on IDC’s scale), and 39% see returns of 5x or more versus 4% of slow adopters.
  • Measurement is the next test. Only 61% of organizations are highly confident they can measure AI’s business value and ROI, versus 93% of Frontier Firms.
  • Governance is in place, but confidence lags. 65% of organizations have an established process to govern agents, yet only 60% have high confidence in addressing AI security and governance risks.
  • Workforce readiness is uneven. 67% say their workforce reports high trust in AI, yet only 20% have a comprehensive, organization-wide skilling strategy.

“Organizations that scale AI value aren’t simply spending more. They manage AI investments, models, agents, governance and skills as one discipline, and that is what turns early results into value they can repeat across the business,” says Kathy Lange, Research Director, AI, Data and Automation Software, IDC.

AI value now reaches well beyond cost savings

Organizations now use AI in 6.5 business areas on average, led by IT infrastructure, cybersecurity and customer service, with the fastest growth in industry-specific uses.

Employee experience, revenue growth, customer experience, innovation and risk reduction now rank nearly even as the places AI strengthens the business. Cost is an important consideration, but it is evaluated alongside accuracy, security, compliance and scalability.

Where scale stalls

66% of leaders say AI has delivered substantial or transformative results, but only 48% are scaling that value across multiple business units. Agents follow the same pattern: 36% of organizations are still piloting them.

The widest gap is people: workforce confidence is running well ahead of the plans to support it. The organizations pulling ahead are closing these gaps by design.

Inside the Frontier Firm

IDC’s maturity scale weighs spending discipline, breadth of use, agent adoption, skills, confidence in managing AI risk and outcomes. On agents specifically, Frontier Firms report a 3.8x return versus 3.0x for slow adopters. These returns are leader-reported, and the research shows association rather than cause.

What they do differently comes down to five behaviors:

  • They invest ahead of plan. 90% of Frontier Firms exceeded their planned AI spend.
  • They deploy AI broadly, across most of the business, not just a few teams.
  • They put agents to work. 96% are rolling out agents at scale, and 53% orchestrate them across workflows.
  • They govern so they can scale. 87% have a process to govern and oversee agents, versus 51% of slow adopters.
  • They build skills everywhere. 80% have an organization-wide AI skilling strategy, versus 3% of slow adopters.

At Bristol Myers Squibb, the RABIT agent “connects the dots across meetings, helping teams make better decisions while reducing administrative follow-up work,” says Lakshman Yerramalla, Director of Portfolio Governance and Delivery for Global Manufacturing Operations. Project managers who use it save up to an estimated 20% of their time.

Four disciplines for scaling AI value

The lesson from Frontier Firms is one I believe every leader can act on: scaling AI value means managing models, agents, governance and measurement as one accountable system. Value and control aren’t a trade-off.

I see the same pattern with customers: the organizations scaling fastest treat AI as a change in how the business runs, not a technology rollout. “The skilling that a lot of companies miss is the business skilling,” says Eric Tabor, Chief Digital Officer, KOHLER. “We also focus on how to dissect processes and convert them into AI workflows.”

Unlock model choice

Redesign workflows around agents

Agents create the most value when work is redesigned around them. The bigger opportunity is what they free people to do more of: leaders point to creativity, innovation and business reinvention (41%), customer-facing work and relationships (39%) and analytical work and data interpretation (39%). Connect agents across processes, with human oversight where it matters.

Govern decisions and actions

Trust is building faster than confidence. Most leaders report high trust in their AI systems, yet fewer are highly confident addressing security and governance risks. As agents take on more of the work, trust has to be earned continuously, and governance has to reach beyond models to keep people in control of what agents decide and do.

Conagra Brands made governance its starting point. “Laying the foundation of proper governance, observability and responsible AI was our first step to engaging our employees with AI,” says Tracy Schaefer, Chief Information Officer, Conagra Brands. “We built a SteerCo to review risk factors, access and identity management.”

Measure and optimize value

Connect investment and performance data to business outcomes, compare how processes perform before and after AI and direct spending where it delivers the most value. With 71% of organizations expecting AI budgets to rise 10% or more in the next 12 months, this discipline will separate leaders from the rest.

Underneath all four disciplines are people. None of it scales without an organization-wide plan to build AI skills. That’s where Frontier Firms are furthest ahead, and it’s where I’d urge every leader to start.

Black & Veatch reached 98% adoption of Microsoft 365 Copilot through deliberate change management, including early-adopter cohorts that surfaced real business use cases. “Our goal is to be a Frontier Firm. The intention is not to stop at pure adoption,” says Mike Adams, Chief Digital Technology Officer, Black & Veatch.

IDC Executive Analyst Shari Lava will lead three sessions at Microsoft Ignite on Nov. 18, including The AI ROI Divide: Why Some Organizations Scale and Others Stall.

What this means for business

The gap that matters now isn’t between companies that use AI and those that don’t. It’s between those getting results in pockets and those turning AI into repeatable value across the business. There are three key ways leaders can step into this kind of transformation.

First, treat AI as business transformation, not a technology rollout. Frontier Firms connect AI to the outcomes that matter most, from growth to customer experience, and manage it as one accountable system. That is the heart of Frontier Transformation, and it’s the work we’re doing alongside our customers every day.

Second, start with your own function. In marketing, we’re applying these same disciplines to our own work: redesigning workflows around agents, setting clear guardrails and measuring what AI actually delivers. Every function can become its own proof point for the rest of the business.

Third, invest in people as much as in technology. Skills are the widest gap in this year’s research, and it’s the one I care about most. The organizations that pull ahead will be the ones where everyone, at every level, has the support to learn, experiment and grow with AI.

The next phase of AI won’t be defined by who uses it. It will be defined by who can scale its value and stay in control. This research gives every leader a benchmark for where they stand today and a clear view of what to do next.

title: Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work
text: If you want to compete, you need to be multi-model. And if you want to take advantage of everything that different AI models have to offer, you need a great harness. But building one that works seamlessly across multiple models and surfaces is incredibly hard. You need to solve for performance, quality, and cost. And then you have to maintain it, which is even harder. Luckily, the GitHub engineering team built a best-in-class, truly multi-model harness , which we’ve adopted company-wide. The Microsoft Copilot harness powers Copilot Code, Copilot Studio, the GitHub Copilot app, the CLI, VS Code, and more. And today, we’re making that harness available through Microsoft Foundry . That gives developers and enterprise customers a fully managed way to build agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. You get the right model for the job without switching the harness or the rest of your tech stack. That frees up your time, energy, and resources to focus on your bottom line. What’s a harness, and why is it hard? If the model supplies the intelligence, the harness is everything around the model. It’s the orchestration layer that gives an agent the right instructions, context, execution environment, and controls to accomplish meaningful work. And a harness worth its salt has support for open standards like MCP and agent skills, as well as agent plugins. This is a fast-moving space. A frontier model today might fall behind tomorrow. And building your own harness or model router to keep up can be painful and slow. Now, you can build on the same harness Microsoft and GitHub ship in our own products, and you don’t have to maintain it. We invest in science and engineering work to continually improve and evolve the harness and ensure high-quality, efficient, and low-cost performance across a range of models and workloads. The benefits compound for us and our customers who use the harness to build and run their own agents. Improve the harness, and every surface it touches benefits. Born in GitHub, battle-tested at enterprise scale The Copilot harness was built by the same GitHub engineers behind new technologies like our multi-model orchestration . And those technologies are only possible because we built our own harness. Designed to be fast, token-efficient, and predictable, it was our original, high-quality harness. And it had the highest satisfaction among our most demanding audience: developers. That’s why we’re standardizing all of our Copilot experiences on the strongest foundation possible. The harness is built to perform across model families , with 20+ frontier models plus bring your own key, so you can use the right model for the right job. Instead of doing the work to keep up with and eval new models, lean on us to intelligently route work to the right model or models based on the task. Our harness is flexible and configurable to any type of app, agent, or service. We recently ported the harness runtime to Rust , which has resulted in industry-leading performance and reductions in both session overhead and time-to-first token. And because the Copilot harness powers surfaces across Microsoft, it’s battle-tested and proven performant at the scale of millions of users and hundreds of real-world use cases. A unified harness lets us ship faster, learn faster, and improve Copilot over time. And because the agents you build in Foundry can run on the same harness we’ve adopted across Microsoft, our continuous harness improvements will benefit your agents, too. Try it yourself The SDK is available to download , or you can run the harness in the cloud, all managed by Foundry. Our platforms remain open and interoperable, so you can continue to bring in any harness and framework you want, too. With the Copilot harness, Microsoft runs the agent loop and sandbox, with governance and optimization built in from day one. You bring the instructions, skills, tools, and model choice. This is an important step towards our vision of a stronger system around the model that preserves choice. It represents the best of GitHub, brought to the Microsoft platform and beyond. We’ll keep pushing the harness forward, so you can focus on what only you can build. title: The platform approach to becoming Frontier
text: Last year at Ignite, we introduced the concept of Frontier Transformation and how it is different from any technology-led pursuit, because it requires us to focus on business outcomes first. It starts with a simple idea: technology was invented to serve humanity, not the other way around. There is no path where this notion of infinite cognitive compute replaces human purpose. Frontier Transformation is an opportunity for a wholesale reinvention of how you think about your unique ideas coming to life and how your organization can thrive in your industry. Over the course of this past year, we have been leading our customers to focus on the three durable traits that are required for successful transformation: human ambition, intelligence and trust. We are taking a platform approach toward enabling the same: Copilot as the place to call home for interacting with AI to empower human ambition; the Microsoft IQ platform to compound and amplify your intelligence from within while protecting your unique differentiation; and Agent 365 to enable Trust and Observability at every layer of the stack so that you can govern, manage, secure and get business value and return out of the capabilities you deliver. Our latest earnings are another important marker on that journey. Behind the numbers are thousands of customers, partners, developers and employees putting AI to work in meaningful ways. We have so many inspiring stories from our customers that highlight these outcomes, and below are some of our favorites. Empowering human ambition with Copilot Volkswagen has scaled Microsoft Copilot to more than 330,000 employees as it expands the role of AI in decision-making and knowledge-based processes across the enterprise. Building on Copilot Chat adoption that reached more than 300,000 monthly active users, employees are now using Copilot with Work IQ for more advanced scenarios, bringing greater organizational context to decision-making and knowledge-based work . Volkswagen is also working with Microsoft to further scale its Intelligent Data Foundation on Microsoft Fabric to make data easier to find, understand and use across the entire company. With this investment, Volkswagen is demonstrating how companies have evolved from using Copilot as a productivity tool to an operating system to empower human ambition. Following a successful pilot, Fujitsu is scaling Microsoft Copilot across its global workforce of approximately 100,000 . Copilot usage has surpassed 90%, and the company is using the tool to connect employees with specialized agents and business systems. AI agents are already automating roughly 75% of initial responses and triage for a service desk that receives nearly 300,000 inquiries annually , while new agents are supporting work across sales, systems engineering, procurement, finance and accounting. As customer zero, Fujitsu is using Copilot as the front door to a multi-agent work environment and using insights from its own AI adoption to better serve its customers. KOHLER is using GitHub Copilot to transform software development, with one organization improving code releases by 25% and reducing error defects by 75%. These engineering breakthroughs are part of a broader effort to embed AI processes across the company, spanning IT, finance, marketing, supply chain and operations. Microsoft Copilot has reached 98% adoption, saving an average of 2 to 5 hours per month as employees are making informed decisions and getting answers faster in the flow of their work . Employees across the company have also created more than 3,000 agents to date, with hundreds active daily . At Krafton , Microsoft Security Copilot and Microsoft Defender XDR are helping the security team respond to a growing volume and complexity of threats. The global gaming company automated key parts of security operations, from alerting and investigation to reporting, combining Microsoft Security solutions with its own systems and data to quickly gather context that helps distinguish real threats from false positives. This approach is having immediate results: security alert recognition time has fallen by approximately 95% to less than one minute, investigation work that previously took tens of minutes now takes about three minutes and roughly 95% of report creation has been automated . By taking on repetitive work, AI is giving Krafton’s security professionals more time to focus on responding to real threats and making critical security decisions. To accelerate discovery across decades of scientific data, NASA is making complex information easier to explore through Microsoft Copilot. NASA employees are using Copilot to sift through massive amounts of academic literature and streamline daily tasks, and specialized assistants are helping researchers navigate complex Earth science data through natural language, extending access to information that once required significant technical expertise. Hydrology Copilot, for example, can analyze variables like precipitation and soil moisture to help communities better understand water conditions, prepare for droughts and anticipate flood risks, while automatically performing calculations and analyses. To transform frontline work, Williams , a US natural gas company, is using Microsoft Copilot to help employees spend less time searching documents and completing manual processes, and more time on critical field operations. Copilot helps teams generate plans, interpret procedures, assess regulatory requirements, troubleshoot issues and complete safety reporting , while employees can create agents tailored to their own workflows. Demonstrating that the person closest to a problem is often the best one to solve it, one operations technician built an anomaly detector using Copilot that compares equipment data against baseline statistics and alerts teams to potential issues before they become costly or dangerous . Since deploying Copilot, AI adoption at Williams has grown from single digits to more than 90%, helping employees accelerate operations, improve reporting and compliance and identify equipment issues earlier. Bristol Myers Squibb has rolled out Microsoft Copilot to 25,000 employees, reaching 96% adoption , and is now putting AI agents to work across everyday use cases such as document review and project management in support of the company’s mission to bring more medicines to more patients faster. One agent, called RABIT, analyzes meeting transcripts, surfaces action items and delivers insights directly within employees’ workflows. Facing rising patient demand and financial pressures, Brown University Health is using Dragon Copilot to give clinicians more time to focus on patients. The health system adopted Dragon Copilot, and an early pilot across 420 clinicians found users spent less time on after-hours documentation and reported lower cognitive burden . Building on that experience, Brown University Health deployed Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio across departments, which led to the creation of more than 24 AI agents to support clinical workflows, hospital policies, patient access and operations . These AI solutions are not only supporting clinicians in the flow of their work but also helping to improve the patient experience and access to care. Microsoft IQ compounds and protects your intelligence BNY has made AI part of how its employees work through Eliza, its in-house AI platform built with Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Copilot and GitHub Copilot – with plans to add Work IQ. More than 300 solutions now run on Eliza, ranging from inquiry management to client onboarding, and 100% of employees have been trained on the platform. Across the bank, that scale is translating into meaningful results: client transaction inquiries are being resolved 80% faster and AI-assisted client onboarding is 20% faster on average . Through the Microsoft CEO Co-Innovation program, BNY also worked with Microsoft to develop an AI research capability with Foundry that investigates complex data issues, analyzes context across multiple sources, identifies likely root causes and recommends next steps, bringing AI-assisted reasoning into processes that have traditionally relied on human investigation alone. Docusign is helping 1.9 million customers across 180 countries turn agreement data into actionable business insights. The company built an Intelligent Agreement Management platform on Microsoft Azure and used Microsoft Foundry to shift from general-purpose models to a system of task-specific models that better understand context . This change allows Docusign to process more than a million agreement documents in a single day, with up to eightfold greater throughput and 90% lower AI processing costs. Foundry also supports a model lifecycle designed for continuous improvement, where processes are fine-tuned before deployment and monitored in production , while also providing the governance and traceability needed to meet enterprise requirements for compliance, visibility and control. Now agreement content is structured data that compounds from within, so organizations can use it to make decisions and automate workflows, knowing their IP is protected. To help marketers create more effective content, Kantar turned decades of proprietary advertising intelligence into action with Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry. Working with Microsoft Frontier Company , Kantar connected its LINK AI platform to its proprietary intelligence, AI models and creative workflows, enabling marketers to evaluate, optimize and generate content before it goes to market. The new approach can process and score large volumes of videos 20x faster while reducing platform operating costs by 4x , helping customers move from insight to action in minutes rather than hours . By bringing its unique intelligence into a continuous loop of observation and improvement, Kantar is creating new ways to help marketers turn insight into better creative and business outcomes. Kinaxis , a Canadian supply chain software company, runs Maestro, its AI-driven supply chain orchestration platform, on Microsoft Azure. Maestro helps businesses make better decisions faster amid constant disruption. It brings together traditionally disparate business data like sales orders, inventory and production capacity with external signals like weather, market shifts and breaking news to give planners a near real-time view of their supply chains . With this unified data foundation, planners and analysts can use predictive AI and optimization models to anticipate demand shifts, evaluate constraints and recommend action, while generative AI agents act as assistants to ask questions, explore scenarios and automate parts of the planning process. With this intelligence in one platform, businesses can understand how disruptions ripple across their interconnected operations, weigh trade-offs and adjust plans as conditions change. Moody’s is making more than a century of credit and risk intelligence directly accessible through Microsoft Copilot, giving customers trusted, protected context for complex decisions. Through a federated connector built using Model Context Protocol, customers can access live, decision-grade Moody’s intelligence through Researcher in Copilot and within Word, Excel and Teams, without copying or exporting the underlying data. A single question can synthesize information across credit ratings, company financials, ownership information and physical risk models, helping customers reach insights in minutes instead of spending hours or days on research and analysis . This brings trusted, connected intelligence directly into workflows where customers make complex decisions. To turn conversations into actionable intelligence at global scale, Plaud , an AI hardware and software company, is using Microsoft Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models and Azure Speech in Foundry Tools to power transcription, summarization and AI inference across long-form audio and multilingual scenarios. Serving more than 2 million users worldwide, Plaud increased transcription accuracy and processing speed by 35% and improved inference performance by 30%, helping professionals turn spoken content into structured outputs and insights . Even as its user base doubled, the company used Foundry’s elastic scaling and flexible deployment models to reduce overall compute costs by 35%, while strengthening its ability to meet security, privacy and compliance requirements across global markets . Rockwell Automation built a Maintenance Copilot using Microsoft Foundry to put decades of manufacturing expertise in the hands of employees . The AI assistant brings together expert knowledge from veteran engineers, manufacturing data and machine manuals, allowing technicians to quickly identify likely causes of equipment issues, see how colleagues have solved similar problems and access step-by-step troubleshooting guidance. At its Singapore factory, the approach has helped reduce machine downtime by 33% and cut servicing and spare-part costs by about 25%. Rockwell estimates it has also reduced the time it takes new workers to learn to troubleshoot hundreds of machines from nine months to three months . With 1.5 billion passengers riding its elevators and escalators every day, TK Elevator knows that every minute of downtime affects how people move through airports, hospitals and offices. Building on a decade of connected-equipment data on Microsoft Azure, the company created AI agents with Microsoft Foundry that brief service technicians before they enter a building, telling them which elevator, which floor, what the issue is and which tools to bring . After each job, a voice agent records the technician’s account of the work in their own words, with no typing, and adds that expertise to a shared record. With 25,000 technicians caring for 1.4 million units worldwide , TK Elevator is turning each technician’s know-how into compounded intelligence every colleague can draw on. Telstra partnered with Microsoft Frontier Company to deploy an AI-powered Migration Payment Agent that helps simplify one of the most complex aspects of customer migration: reconciling billing and payments across legacy and new platforms. The agent uses intelligence across these systems to proactively identify inconsistencies, recommend corrective actions and create enriched cases for human review, combining AI-driven insights with human-in-the-loop validation to maintain operational trust and governance. Already supporting more than 272,000 service migrations and delivering recommendations at 95%+ accuracy in production , the solution demonstrates how Telstra is applying agentic AI at enterprise scale to transform complex operations, improve customer outcomes and build reusable AI capabilities while compounding and protecting Telstra’s operational intelligence. Agent 365 observes AI solutions across the stack To advance its transformation into an AI-powered organization, Manulife is adopting Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite, expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 30,000 employees and leveraging Microsoft Agent 365 to govern, manage and secure AI agents at enterprise scale . With Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry supporting its global enterprise AI platform, Manulife is building a foundation for teams to develop and deploy AI and agentic solutions while maintaining standards for quality, security and cost efficiency. AI is already delivering impact across the business, from generative AI solutions supporting more than 110 million customer calls annually to developers increasing productivity by 30% with assisted and autonomous AI capabilities . With agentic solutions and AI-powered workflows already in production, Manulife is creating the foundation to scale AI responsibly across its global operations and accelerate its next phase of enterprise transformation. Insight Enterprises , a leading solutions integrator and top Microsoft partner, is using Microsoft Agent 365 to govern AI agents at scale . Last year at Ignite, we introduced the concept of Frontier Transformation and how it is different from any technology-led pursuit, because it requires us to focus on business outcomes first. It starts with a simple idea: technology was invented to serve humanity, not the other way around. There is no path where this notion of infinite cognitive compute replaces human purpose. Frontier Transformation is an opportunity for a wholesale reinvention of how you think about your unique ideas coming to life and how your organization can thrive in your industry.

Over the course of this past year, we have been leading our customers to focus on the three durable traits that are required for successful transformation: human ambition, intelligence and trust. We are taking a platform approach toward enabling the same: Copilot as the place to call home for interacting with AI to empower human ambition; the Microsoft IQ platform to compound and amplify your intelligence from within while protecting your unique differentiation; and Agent 365 to enable Trust and Observability at every layer of the stack so that you can govern, manage, secure and get business value and return out of the capabilities you deliver.

Our latest earnings are another important marker on that journey. Behind the numbers are thousands of customers, partners, developers and employees putting AI to work in meaningful ways. We have so many inspiring stories from our customers that highlight these outcomes, and below are some of our favorites.

Volkswagen has scaled Microsoft Copilot to more than 330,000 employees as it expands the role of AI in decision-making and knowledge-based processes across the enterprise. Building on Copilot Chat adoption that reached more than 300,000 monthly active users, employees are now using Copilot with Work IQ for more advanced scenarios, bringing greater organizational context to decision-making and knowledge-based work. With this investment, Volkswagen is demonstrating how companies have evolved from using Copilot as a productivity tool to an operating system to empower human ambition.

Following a successful pilot, Fujitsu is scaling Microsoft Copilot across its global workforce of approximately 100,000. Copilot usage has surpassed 90%, and the company is using the tool to connect employees with specialized agents and business systems. AI agents are already automating roughly 75% of initial responses and triage for a service desk that receives nearly 300,000 inquiries annually, while new agents are supporting work across sales, systems engineering, procurement, finance and accounting. As customer zero, Fujitsu is using Copilot as the front door to a multi-agent work environment and using insights from its own AI adoption to better serve its customers.

KOHLER is using GitHub Copilot to transform software development, with one organization improving code releases by 25% and reducing error defects by 75%. These engineering breakthroughs are part of a broader effort to embed AI processes across the company, spanning IT, finance, marketing, supply chain and operations. Microsoft Copilot has reached 98% adoption, saving an average of 2 to 5 hours per month as employees are making informed decisions and getting answers faster in the flow of their work. Employees across the company have also created more than 3,000 agents to date, with hundreds active daily.

At Krafton, Microsoft Security Copilot and Microsoft Defender XDR are helping the security team respond to a growing volume and complexity of threats. The global gaming company automated key parts of security operations, from alerting and investigation to reporting, combining Microsoft Security solutions with its own systems and data to quickly gather context that helps distinguish real threats from false positives. This approach is having immediate results: security alert recognition time has fallen by approximately 95% to less than one minute, investigation work that previously took tens of minutes now takes about three minutes and roughly 95% of report creation has been automated. By taking on repetitive work, AI is giving Krafton’s security professionals more time to focus on responding to real threats and making critical security decisions.

This change allows Docusign to process more than a million agreement documents in a single day, with up to eightfold greater throughput and 90% lower AI processing costs. Foundry also supports a model lifecycle designed for continuous improvement, where processes are fine-tuned before deployment and monitored in production, while also providing the governance and traceability needed to meet enterprise requirements for compliance, visibility and control. Now agreement content is structured data that compounds from within, so organizations can use it to make decisions and automate workflows, knowing their IP is protected.

With this unified data foundation, planners and analysts can use predictive AI and optimization models to anticipate demand shifts, evaluate constraints and recommend action, while generative AI agents act as assistants to ask questions, explore scenarios and automate parts of the planning process. With this intelligence in one platform, businesses can understand how disruptions ripple across their interconnected operations, weigh trade-offs and adjust plans as conditions change.

title: Introducing a Voluntary Exit Offer
text: Amy Coleman, Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer, shared the below communication with Microsoft employees today. Today, we’re introducing a new Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) to eligible employees within participating organizations. This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs. The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter. This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program. What employees should know This offer will be available to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 and below . This is a time-limited, voluntary program that gives those who are eligible the opportunity to leave Microsoft with financial support and career planning resources. Some organizations are providing the Voluntary Exit Offer, and some are not. Participation varies based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs. Eligible employees will receive an email with a link to their Voluntary Exit Offer details within the next few hours. Looking ahead The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We’ll learn from it. At the same time, we’ll keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft. There is no one-size-fits-all approach for every team or every employee. These are a few of the ways we’re trying to meet different business needs while continuing to create opportunities for our own people to grow and contribute. My promise is to continue to provide clarity, listen and learn and keep improving. Thank you for everything you continue to do for our customers, Microsoft and for one another.
