title: Advancing digital sovereignty with greater control and choice
text: Across my conversations with leaders in government, critical infrastructure and regulated industries, one priority consistently rises to the top: putting technology to work on their most important systems while maintaining the control those systems require. This challenge is becoming more important as advanced cloud and AI capabilities move into public services, regulated processes and essential operations. Organizations are considering more than where data resides. They also seek to understand who can access and operate their systems, how sensitive digital assets remain protected, which technology dependencies matter most and whether critical services can continue as regulatory, geopolitical, security or network conditions change. Digital sovereignty should give organizations greater control and security over the technology they depend on, while continuing to innovate. Last year, we introduced Microsoft Sovereign Cloud to give customers more choice in how they address these requirements. Since then, we have continued to turn our commitments into practical capabilities across public cloud and customer-operated environments, while expanding how we enable partners to address sovereignty requirements in their local markets. Today, we are sharing the next stage of that work. YouTube Video Click here to load media A continuum of control, built around the workload Our approach to digital sovereignty starts with the workload. Each workload carries different requirements for data, operations, technology dependencies, continuity and risk. Microsoft Sovereign Cloud is designed to make it easier for organizations to apply the appropriate level of control to each workload without forcing every application into the same deployment model. Those needs can vary widely across organizations. A public-facing digital service may benefit from the scale and pace of innovation in the public cloud. A system supporting essential operations may need to continue running locally if connectivity is disrupted. An AI workload handling highly sensitive data may require models, data and processing to remain within a customer-controlled environment. Microsoft Sovereign Cloud is designed around this workload-based approach, providing a continuum of management, control and options across Sovereign Public Cloud, Sovereign Private Cloud and the Sovereign Partner Ecosystem. Organizations can apply the level of control appropriate to each workload while maintaining a consistent approach to governance and operations across their digital estate. Sovereign Public Cloud adds capabilities for workloads that require greater control and transparency while continuing to benefit from the scale and innovation of Azure. Sovereign Private Cloud extends cloud capabilities into customer-operated environments, including connected and disconnected operations. The Sovereign Partner Ecosystem broadens the continuum through independently operated environments, specialized partners, locally relevant expertise and technologies that support customers’ sovereignty requirements. These are not isolated destinations. Customers can combine public cloud, private cloud and partner capabilities across their digital estate, applying different levels of control to different workloads as their operating needs evolve. Making control more visible in Sovereign Public Cloud For many workloads, the public cloud provides a combination of scale, innovation, integrated security and compliance. Organizations can benefit from these capabilities while applying additional sovereignty controls for residency, confidentiality, operator access, policy and continuity. Our work in Sovereign Public Cloud makes these controls easier to understand, apply and demonstrate. Sovereign Control Panel , entering public preview at Microsoft Ignite, brings these signals together in a unified Azure portal experience. It helps organizations understand their sovereignty posture, apply and manage controls, identify gaps and risks and take action to address them. It also supports business continuity readiness by helping customers understand workload dependencies and assess portability across operating environments when required. This visibility complements controls across the operator-access lifecycle. Just-in-time Access and Customer Lockbox give customers additional control over access to their environments. For customers in the European Union (EU) and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), we are rolling out Data Guardian , which adds European-resident oversight by a trusted EU partner for qualifying Microsoft engineer remote access to in-scope production systems. Production Touch Ledger , also launched with phased rollout in the EU and EFTA, creates tamper-evident records of that access and the actions performed. Azure Key Vault Managed Hardware Security Module (HSM) already gives customers dedicated, single-tenant protection and control over the encryption keys used by supported Azure services. Last year, we committed to extending that control beyond Microsoft infrastructure. External key management with Azure Managed HSM is now generally available, allowing customers to keep the root encryption key in hardware they own and operate on-premises or through a trusted third party. This gives organizations another option for workloads that require physical control of key hardware outside Microsoft infrastructure. Azure confidential computing helps protect supported data while it is processed in a hardware-based and attested trusted execution environment. We are also increasing transparency into the technologies that underpin that trust. Azure Confidential Clean Rooms , now in limited preview, applies confidential computing to approved multiparty collaboration, allowing participants to analyze shared sensitive data while limiting broader exposure of the underlying information. Together, these capabilities provide additional technical and operational controls that can support a broader digital sovereignty strategy aligned to an organization’s legal, policy, security, resilience and business requirements. Designing for resilience and operational independence For some workloads, digital sovereignty also means maintaining critical operations as connectivity, geopolitical and operating conditions change. Resilience must be designed from the start so essential workloads can continue operating through disruption. To help customers prepare for these scenarios, we are publishing new sovereign business continuity guidance and architecture patterns . These resources help organizations translate resilience requirements into architectures they can plan, implement and test before they are needed. For many workloads, the scale and geographic reach of the public cloud provide a strong foundation for resilience across locations and operating conditions. For workloads that require greater operational independence, Sovereign Private Cloud extends that continuum into customer-operated environments. It supports connected and disconnected operating models. The ability to transition workloads from connected to disconnected operations is entering public preview, giving organizations greater flexibility to sustain critical services as connectivity and operating requirements change. Bringing more of the application lifecycle under local control Operational independence requires more than infrastructure. Increasingly, organizations need data, development tools, model capabilities and productivity services their applications depend on to operate within the same customer-controlled environment. Sovereign Private Cloud, built on Azure Local, extends Microsoft cloud capabilities into environments that customers operate and control. SQL Server on Azure Local is already generally available for connected and disconnected deployments. DocumentDB and Blob Storage on Azure Local are both entering public preview, giving organizations more choice in how they run and manage critical data within customer-controlled environments. GitHub Enterprise Local will become generally available at Microsoft Ignite as a validated GitHub Enterprise Server appliance on Azure Local, helping organizations keep repositories, code and development artifacts under local control. Developers can also use GitHub Copilot with locally hosted models for inference, bringing AI-assisted development closer to their code and data within the environments they control. The local application environment is expanding with Foundry Local . At Ignite, Foundry Local will become generally available for connected and disconnected operations on Azure Local, with an expanded model catalog that includes Microsoft, partner, open-weight and open-source models. Local inference and agentic retrieval will also enable users to interact with local enterprise data using natural language and receive responses grounded in that data. Integration with Microsoft 365 Local , available in preview for approved customers, extends this functionality to locally operated Microsoft SharePoint and Exchange servers. Confidential virtual machines on Azure Local are generally available, extending confidential computing capabilities to customer-controlled infrastructure. Hardware-encrypted memory and hardware-based isolation help protect sensitive data while it is being processed. Workload attestation adds assurance before sensitive data or keys are released. For regulated, sensitive and mission-critical workloads, these safeguards provide another layer of protection while giving organizations greater control over where their data and applications run. Azure Local will support multitenancy , allowing organizations to separate resources, governance and management across multiple tenants while sharing the underlying infrastructure. This significantly expands what customers with distinct business units or security boundaries can achieve with Sovereign Private Cloud. Multitenancy also creates new opportunities for local operators and service providers to deliver differentiated sovereign cloud services on Azure Local infrastructure. These additions bring more of the application lifecycle under local control, spanning data, development, productivity, AI and operations. Organizations can determine what runs locally based on the requirements of each workload. Extending the continuum through partners Navigating sovereignty is increasingly complex. Regulatory, security, operational and business requirements vary across countries, industries and workloads. Organizations must translate these needs into technology and operating models that work in their local context. Meeting these needs often requires a combination of technology, local operating authority, sector expertise and specialized solutions. The Sovereign Partner Ecosystem broadens the ways customers can address these requirements. National Partner Clouds , including Bleu Cloud in France and Delos Cloud in Germany, provide independently operated environments for customers that require a different ownership and operating model. Software partners can enhance Azure Local environments with capabilities across security, identity, observability, backup and recovery, migration, data, networking and applications. Digital sovereignty specialized partners combine Microsoft technologies with local knowledge and implementation expertise. Platform co-innovation partners expand infrastructure choice from datacenter to the edge. This ecosystem gives customers the flexibility to combine technology, operating models and trusted expertise based on the requirements of each workload. The next chapter of digital sovereignty AI is amplifying both the opportunity and the impact of technology choices. As AI systems and agents interact with sensitive data, business processes and essential infrastructure, they also expand the security considerations organizations need to manage. Organizations need clear control over where these systems run, who can operate them, what actions they can take and how critical services continue when conditions change. Microsoft Sovereign Cloud brings these choices together as a continuum of control across the public cloud, customer-operated environments and our partner ecosystem. It gives organizations the flexibility to apply the appropriate level of control to each workload while continuing to benefit from cloud capabilities and ongoing innovation. We will continue to expand this continuum so organizations can innovate with cloud and AI while maintaining the control, confidentiality, resilience and operational authority their most important workloads require. Douglas Phillips leads global engineering efforts for Microsoft’s specialized, sovereign and private clouds. He is responsible for Microsoft’s global strategy, products and operations that bring Microsoft’s industry-leading solutions, including Azure, our adaptive cloud portfolio and Microsoft 365 collaboration suite, to customers with additional sovereignty, security, edge and compliance requirements. Sovereign Control Panel, entering public preview at Microsoft Ignite, brings these signals together in a unified Azure portal experience. It helps organizations understand their sovereignty posture, apply and manage controls, identify gaps and risks and take action to address them. It also supports business continuity readiness by helping customers understand workload dependencies and assess portability across operating environments when required.

This visibility complements controls across the operator-access lifecycle. Just-in-time Access and Customer Lockbox give customers additional control over access to their environments. For customers in the European Union (EU) and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), we are rolling out Data Guardian, which adds European-resident oversight by a trusted EU partner for qualifying Microsoft engineer remote access to in-scope production systems. Production Touch Ledger, also launched with phased rollout in the EU and EFTA, creates tamper-evident records of that access and the actions performed.

Azure Key Vault Managed Hardware Security Module (HSM) already gives customers dedicated, single-tenant protection and control over the encryption keys used by supported Azure services. Last year, we committed to extending that control beyond Microsoft infrastructure. External key management with Azure Managed HSM is now generally available, allowing customers to keep the root encryption key in hardware they own and operate on-premises or through a trusted third party. This gives organizations another option for workloads that require physical control of key hardware outside Microsoft infrastructure.

Azure confidential computing helps protect supported data while it is processed in a hardware-based and attested trusted execution environment. We are also increasing transparency into the technologies that underpin that trust. Azure Confidential Clean Rooms, now in limited preview, applies confidential computing to approved multiparty collaboration, allowing participants to analyze shared sensitive data while limiting broader exposure of the underlying information.

Together, these capabilities provide additional technical and operational controls that can support a broader digital sovereignty strategy aligned to an organization’s legal, policy, security, resilience and business requirements.

Designing for resilience and operational independence

For some workloads, digital sovereignty also means maintaining critical operations as connectivity, geopolitical and operating conditions change. Resilience must be designed from the start so essential workloads can continue operating through disruption.

To help customers prepare for these scenarios, we are publishing new sovereign business continuity guidance and architecture patterns. These resources help organizations translate resilience requirements into architectures they can plan, implement and test before they are needed.

For many workloads, the scale and geographic reach of the public cloud provide a strong foundation for resilience across locations and operating conditions. For workloads that require greater operational independence, Sovereign Private Cloud extends that continuum into customer-operated environments. It supports connected and disconnected operating models. The ability to transition workloads from connected to disconnected operations is entering public preview, giving organizations greater flexibility to sustain critical services as connectivity and operating requirements change.

Bringing more of the application lifecycle under local control

Operational independence requires more than infrastructure. Increasingly, organizations need data, development tools, model capabilities and productivity services their applications depend on to operate within the same customer-controlled environment.

Sovereign Private Cloud, built on Azure Local, extends Microsoft cloud capabilities into environments that customers operate and control. SQL Server on Azure Local is already generally available for connected and disconnected deployments. DocumentDB and Blob Storage on Azure Local are both entering public preview, giving organizations more choice in how they run and manage critical data within customer-controlled environments.

GitHub Enterprise Local will become generally available at Microsoft Ignite as a validated GitHub Enterprise Server appliance on Azure Local, helping organizations keep repositories, code and development artifacts under local control. Developers can also use GitHub Copilot with locally hosted models for inference, bringing AI-assisted development closer to their code and data within the environments they control.

The local application environment is expanding with Foundry Local. At Ignite, Foundry Local will become generally available for connected and disconnected operations on Azure Local, with an expanded model catalog that includes Microsoft, partner, open-weight and open-source models. Local inference and agentic retrieval will also enable users to interact with local enterprise data using natural language and receive responses grounded in that data. Integration with Microsoft 365 Local, available in preview for approved customers, extends this functionality to locally operated Microsoft SharePoint and Exchange servers.

Confidential virtual machines on Azure Local are generally available, extending confidential computing capabilities to customer-controlled infrastructure. Hardware-encrypted memory and hardware-based isolation help protect sensitive data while it is being processed. Workload attestation adds assurance before sensitive data or keys are released. For regulated, sensitive and mission-critical workloads, these safeguards provide another layer of protection while giving organizations greater control over where their data and applications run.

Azure Local will support multitenancy, allowing organizations to separate resources, governance and management across multiple tenants while sharing the underlying infrastructure. This significantly expands what customers with distinct business units or security boundaries can achieve with Sovereign Private Cloud. Multitenancy also creates new opportunities for local operators and service providers to deliver differentiated sovereign cloud services on Azure Local infrastructure.

These additions bring more of the application lifecycle under local control, spanning data, development, productivity, AI and operations. Organizations can determine what runs locally based on the requirements of each workload.

Extending the continuum through partners

 

Navigating sovereignty is increasingly complex. Regulatory, security, operational and business requirements vary across countries, industries and workloads. Organizations must translate these needs into technology and operating models that work in their local context. Meeting these needs often requires a combination of technology, local operating authority, sector expertise and specialized solutions.

The Sovereign Partner Ecosystem broadens the ways customers can address these requirements. National Partner Clouds, including Bleu Cloud in France and Delos Cloud in Germany, provide independently operated environments for customers that require a different ownership and operating model. Software partners can enhance Azure Local environments with capabilities across security, identity, observability, backup and recovery, migration, data, networking and applications. Digital sovereignty specialized partners combine Microsoft technologies with local knowledge and implementation expertise. Platform co-innovation partners expand infrastructure choice from datacenter to the edge.

This ecosystem gives customers the flexibility to combine technology, operating models and trusted expertise based on the requirements of each workload.

The next chapter of digital sovereignty

AI is amplifying both the opportunity and the impact of technology choices. As AI systems and agents interact with sensitive data, business processes and essential infrastructure, they also expand the security considerations organizations need to manage. Organizations need clear control over where these systems run, who can operate them, what actions they can take and how critical services continue when conditions change.

Microsoft Sovereign Cloud brings these choices together as a continuum of control across the public cloud, customer-operated environments and our partner ecosystem. It gives organizations the flexibility to apply the appropriate level of control to each workload while continuing to benefit from cloud capabilities and ongoing innovation.

We will continue to expand this continuum so organizations can innovate with cloud and AI while maintaining the control, confidentiality, resilience and operational authority their most important workloads require.

title: Securing the agentic insider
text: In the last few months, concerns have arisen about AI safety as a growing number of incidents were publicly disclosed. These incidents exposed how powerful models have become and how they represent a significant threat if not handled well. And with the global race on innovation, the challenge will compound as models become even more powerful. While most have been worried about threat actors using powerful models to attack, the focus has been less on agents within our own walls. Since we were the ones who deployed agents internally for our companies, we implicitly trusted our agents. Unfortunately, frontier models, regardless of their origin, cannot be trusted . This is not because models are inherently malicious. Models have been trained to attain results, which often leads to reward hacking, and models are not optimized around organizational norms or judgment. Agents are unpredictable. They will adapt as the context changes, may not behave as intended and will collaborate and collude with other agents to reach their objectives, without needing to be compromised. Agents have been unleashed in the enterprise, at scale, and their numbers are growing rapidly. These agents are frequently overprivileged, have access to data, tools and systems and can take actions and make decisions in critical processes. They have become active participants in the enterprise. They are agentic insiders. Monitoring and securing those agents must become continuous. We need to understand in real time what the agents are doing and what risks those actions create, and we need to adjust their ability to act accordingly. To manage and control these insiders, we will need Guardian Agents — an established industry term — that watch and moderate every action of every agent, before it happens, 24/7. An agent brings together a model, a harness that orchestrates its work, an action space of tools and resources and a runtime in which it executes. Securing agents requires protection across multiple layers: identity, permissions, data, endpoints, network, cloud and runtime. In July, we announced Project Perception , an agentic security system that uses our new cyber stack and teams of red, blue and green agents to help defenders act with speed, while defending against AI driven attacks from outside of the enterprise. The same cyber stack is also directly applicable to managing and governing the agentic insiders that run in the enterprise. Project Perception can be leveraged to contain agentic insiders, implementing deterministic controls on non-deterministic intelligence: Sensors/Signals/Actuators: bring together signals across the various sensors (identity, data, cloud, endpoint, network, runtime) to discover agents in the enterprise and bring them under management by assigning an identity, container and set of policy and permissions . Context: use those signals to compute, dynamically , the risk associated with what the agents are attempting to do. Harness/agents/models: based on dynamic agent risk , a team of Guardian Agents , with green and blue agents, actively and continually supervise every action of every agent and surgically respond as the risk profile increases, in real time. This is where agentic security changes the equation for security practitioners. Project Perception can supervise in real time while providing traceability for practitioners to examine what happened, understand why the risk emerged and apply the judgment needed to update their security system accordingly. Agentic security provides speed . Practitioners provide judgment . That is how defenders begin operating at the same speed as the systems they are protecting against. Today, security systems can reliably observe the actions of the agents. Those signals are essential and tell us what we need to contain. Our security controls should increasingly be able to ask not only “What is happening?” but also “Why is it happening?” Is this consistent with the intent of the task?” This will require greater transparency into the model itself, not only the input and output tokens, but the thinking and chain of thought tokens. Only then can we truly understand whether the model’s intent is aligned with the purpose of the agent. Model transparency will not replace containment. It will make containment smarter and stronger . And it will allow us to better inform accountability and traceability. This needs to be the next step in securing agentic insiders. With Project Perception, you can get started today on the journey to secure your agentic insiders . There should not be a choice between innovation and safety. Hayete Gallot leads Microsoft’s work to help organizations operate securely in an AI-driven world. Her scope includes identity, threat protection, compliance and data security at global scale. raw_content:
In the last few months, concerns have arisen about AI safety as a growing number of incidents were publicly disclosed. These incidents exposed how powerful models have become and how they represent a significant threat if not handled well. And with the global race on innovation, the challenge will compound as models become even more powerful.

While most have been worried about threat actors using powerful models to attack, the focus has been less on agents within our own walls. Since we were the ones who deployed agents internally for our companies, we implicitly trusted our agents.

Unfortunately, frontier models, regardless of their origin, cannot be trusted. This is not because models are inherently malicious. Models have been trained to attain results, which often leads to reward hacking, and models are not optimized around organizational norms or judgment. Agents are unpredictable. They will adapt as the context changes, may not behave as intended and will collaborate and collude with other agents to reach their objectives, without needing to be compromised.

Agents have been unleashed in the enterprise, at scale, and their numbers are growing rapidly. These agents are frequently overprivileged, have access to data, tools and systems and can take actions and make decisions in critical processes. They have become active participants in the enterprise.

They are agentic insiders.

Monitoring and securing those agents must become continuous. We need to understand in real time what the agents are doing and what risks those actions create, and we need to adjust their ability to act accordingly.

To manage and control these insiders, we will need Guardian Agents — an established industry term — that watch and moderate every action of every agent, before it happens, 24/7.

An agent brings together a model, a harness that orchestrates its work, an action space of tools and resources and a runtime in which it executes. Securing agents requires protection across multiple layers: identity, permissions, data, endpoints, network, cloud and runtime.

In July, we announced Project Perception, an agentic security system that uses our new cyber stack and teams of red, blue and green agents to help defenders act with speed, while defending against AI driven attacks from outside of the enterprise.

The same cyber stack is also directly applicable to managing and governing the agentic insiders that run in the enterprise.

Project Perception can be leveraged to contain agentic insiders, implementing deterministic controls on non-deterministic intelligence:

  • Sensors/Signals/Actuators: bring together signals across the various sensors (identity, data, cloud, endpoint, network, runtime) to discover agents in the enterprise and bring them under management by assigning an identity, container and set of policy and permissions.
  • Context: use those signals to compute, dynamically, the risk associated with what the agents are attempting to do.
  • Harness/agents/models: based on dynamic agent risk, a team of Guardian Agents, with green and blue agents, actively and continually supervise every action of every agent and surgically respond as the risk profile increases, in real time.

This is where agentic security changes the equation for security practitioners.

Project Perception can supervise in real time while providing traceability for practitioners to examine what happened, understand why the risk emerged and apply the judgment needed to update their security system accordingly. Agentic security provides speed. Practitioners provide judgment. That is how defenders begin operating at the same speed as the systems they are protecting against.

Today, security systems can reliably observe the actions of the agents. Those signals are essential and tell us what we need to contain. Our security controls should increasingly be able to ask not only “What is happening?” but also “Why is it happening?” Is this consistent with the intent of the task?” This will require greater transparency into the model itself, not only the input and output tokens, but the thinking and chain of thought tokens. Only then can we truly understand whether the model’s intent is aligned with the purpose of the agent. Model transparency will not replace containment. It will make containment smarter and stronger. And it will allow us to better inform accountability and traceability. This needs to be the next step in securing agentic insiders.

With Project Perception, you can get started today on the journey to secure your agentic insiders. There should not be a choice between innovation and safety.

Hayete Gallot leads Microsoft’s work to help organizations operate securely in an AI-driven world. Her scope includes identity, threat protection, compliance and data security at global scale.

title: Microsoft to expand Azure Maia system to multi-gigawatt deployments
text: Azure Maia 200 now in production; Azure Maia 300 coming in 2027 As we move into the era of Super Intelligence, Microsoft is entering a new phase of infrastructure. We will scale our Azure Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027, making Maia the primary inference system for Microsoft products and services. The multigenerational Azure Maia program has become a foundational element of Microsoft’s AI infrastructure strategy. Maia 200 is now serving Microsoft production workloads, including Microsoft Copilot , and supporting the MAI team as they develop next-generation models, with GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Foundry to follow by end of year. Across these workloads, Maia 200 runs OpenAI models , Microsoft’s own MAI models and leading open-source model families. Insights from the scale of Microsoft’s AI services allow for unique co-design between hardware systems and software applications to optimize real-world use cases across enterprise applications and industry scenarios. Maia 300 is a complete intelligent system designed for the new types of AI workloads emerging today: Long-context reasoning, latency-sensitive conversational experiences and sustained, multi-step agentic tasks. By improving efficiency across the system, we expect Maia 300 to deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt compared to leading GPU-based systems. And in a full 96-accelerator configuration, it delivers up to 7x the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200. YouTube Video Click here to load media Maia 200: Driving the workloads that Microsoft runs at scale The Azure Maia system is designed around the real-world workloads Microsoft runs at scale and the models we expect to build in the years ahead. Because silicon development takes years, our software and hardware teams collaborate early to anticipate architectures, scale and capabilities, translating those requirements into greater memory capacity, higher bandwidth and more accelerators operating as a single system. That co-engineering is already delivering measurable efficiency gains. Maia 200 is deploying across the United States, Europe and Australia and delivering up to 1.7x more tokens per watt for built-in AI capabilities in Microsoft Teams, Copilot and Cowork experiences compared with leading GPU infrastructure. Experience running our AI models and services on Maia 200 directly informed the design of Maia 300. Together, the two generations are designed to support a broad set of additional Microsoft’s AI services: multi-step agentic work that will help GitHub deliver coding experiences more efficiently; cloud-scale model serving that will help Microsoft Foundry support diverse architectures and deployment environments; inference and data generation for the MAI team; and latency-sensitive interactions that will help Dragon Copilot scale workflows and reduce clinicians’ administrative burden. Maia 300: Scaling more useful AI within every megawatt AI is becoming a foundational layer of every application, workflow and business process. As enterprises move beyond chat experiences to systems of agents that can reason, act and collaborate, AI infrastructure must deliver intelligence securely and efficiently at scale while continuously adapting as models and workloads evolve. As the third generation of our Azure Maia program, Maia 300 is designed with an inference-first architecture optimized for long-context, memory-intensive and decode-heavy AI workloads. This involves balancing compute, memory bandwidth, networking and power efficiency at cloud scale. Azure Maia 300 system Key capabilities of the Maia 300 system include: Less data movement, more useful compute: Moving data efficiently, rather than raw compute power, is increasingly the bottleneck in large inference systems. Maia 300’s software-defined dataflow architecture and AI-assisted kernel optimization work together to maximize locality, reduce data movement and improve utilization across compute, memory and networking resources. By treating dataflow as a first-class design principle, Maia 300 delivers a significant performance-per-watt advantage over traditional GPU architectures. Higher memory bandwidth within every watt: As AI workloads become increasingly context and memory-bound, Maia 300 delivers industry-leading HBM bandwidth per watt. Eight HBM4 stacks provide 18.0 TB/s of peak memory bandwidth within a 950-watt TDP, enabling efficient execution of large models and long-context workloads. Specialized kernel support uses on-die SRAM as a software-managed scratchpad, reducing pressure on HBM. Chiplet architecture for enhanced efficiency: A new multi-chiplet architecture separates compute, memory-controller and I/O functions, improving efficiency, scalability and cost structure. Compute chiplets are built on TSMC’s N2P process node to maximize performance-per-watt. Larger context, richer intelligence: By designing for advanced low-precision formats, including enhanced MXFP4, Maia 300 reduces memory and bandwidth requirements for both computation and KV-cache storage. The result is larger context windows, higher throughput and improved model efficiency within the same power envelope. Scale-up networking at datacenter scale: Maia 300 treats networking as a seamless extension of the software-defined dataflow architecture. Rather than moving data through separate communication layers, dataflow operations span compute, memory and network resources as a single system. High-bandwidth interconnects between Maia accelerators are optimized for tensor parallelism, while a custom AI transport delivers performant and reliable scale-up communication across accelerators and racks. The AI-optimized transport leverages Ethernet-based networking infrastructure to enable a unified topology that scales efficiently from a single rack to datacenter-scale deployments. Higher AI throughput from every rack: Maia 300 rack systems bring together 96 accelerators within a 167-kilowatt power envelope, delivering 27.6 TB of HBM capacity and 1.7 PB/s of aggregate HBM bandwidth across a high-speed scale-up domain. That density allows Microsoft to serve more simultaneous AI interactions and larger workloads from each rack, improving datacenter capacity and the economics of expanding AI services. Maia 300 will begin production deployments in 2027. For more information on Maia 300 architectural details, read our technical paper . Maia 300 at a glance Azure Maia is at the heart of our Frontier Transformation The future will not be defined by a single model or a single piece of silicon or a single innovation. Model and silicon choice are inherent in our vision for Frontier Transformation. Our focus is on developing responsible, affordable and scalable platforms that will help everyone amplify their intelligence to drive breakthrough outcomes that matter for them. Microsoft is unique because we are able to optimize from silicon to systems to agent on an open, heterogenous and model diverse platform our customers can count on for their AI transformation, today and in the years ahead. This platform is at the heart of Frontier Transformation, and Azure Maia is a foundational component of our approach to expand access, accelerate innovation and help customers capture more value from AI. Next month at Microsoft Ignite 2026 in San Francisco and online we’re looking forward to sharing more information on our strategy, technology adoption trends and success in Frontier Transformation. For more details, photos and videos, visit our Maia 300 site . Scott Guthrie is responsible for a set of hyperscale cloud computing solutions and services including Azure, Microsoft’s cloud computing platform, generative AI solutions, data platforms and information and cybersecurity. These platforms and services help organizations across the globe solve urgent challenges — and transform for the future. title: Microsoft 365 and LinkedIn leadership update
text: Satya Nadella, Chairman and CEO, and Ryan Roslansky, Executive Vice President of LinkedIn and Microsoft 365 , shared the below communications with Microsoft and LinkedIn employees this morning. SATYA NADELLA MESSAGE After nearly 18 years at LinkedIn and Microsoft, Ryan Roslansky has decided to leave Microsoft and embark on his next chapter. As Ryan and I have been discussing our roadmap and work ahead, we felt this was the right moment for this change. Ryan will stay through the end of the calendar year as an advisor to me and will support on the transition. Ryan leaves the organization in a strong position. With Copilot, we are executing rapidly against our vision to build a new OS for work that spans every model, every form factor, and every task, with Office fully embedded in Copilot and vice versa! Over the past year, Ryan’s team has done critical work bringing together the product, engineering, and design foundations that have made this next phase possible. Last week’s launch was an important milestone in that journey, and the strong response from customers, partners, and the broader ecosystem reinforced both how far we’ve come and how much opportunity remains ahead. At LinkedIn, we remain focused on our core vision of creating economic opportunity for every member of the global workforce, helping our 1.3 billion members access the knowledge, insights, and opportunities they need to navigate rapidly changing professional and labor markets. Effective today we will make the following changes: Sumit Chauhan and Lan Ye will report to Charles Lamanna. Jon Friedman will report to Jacob Andreou. Dan Shapero will continue as CEO of LinkedIn and Mohak Shroff will continue in his role, both reporting to me. Over his nearly two decades at Microsoft, Ryan has helped shape how people around the world find opportunity, build their careers, and get their work done. I’ve always appreciated his clarity of thinking and I’m deeply grateful for everything Ryan has built, for the leaders and teams he has developed, and for his friendship and counsel. Please join me in thanking Ryan for his extraordinary contributions to LinkedIn and Microsoft, and in wishing him the very best in what comes next. Satya RYAN ROSLANSKY MESSAGE Team, In 1996, as a college freshman, I taught myself to code so a few friends and I could help other students find a place to live around campus. I didn’t know much. I did know the internet was about to change how people found things, and I wanted to be as close to that as possible. In 2009, Jeff Weiner made me his first hire at LinkedIn. I’ve spent the nearly 18 years since working on a much bigger version of that same idea: helping people find opportunity, and then helping them do great work once they have it. This has (obviously) been the best professional experience of my life. As a product manager, I got to build dozens of features that are still around today (some good, some not so good!). When I became CEO in 2020, the world was months into a pandemic that changed what work even meant. Nobody hands you a playbook for that. This team wrote one anyway. Since then, LinkedIn has passed a billion members and nearly tripled its business, and every bit of that belongs to the people who built it. Last year, Satya asked me to help build the future of M365. Once again, the old rules didn’t apply. AI was rapidly changing how professionals work, and the world’s largest productivity suite needed to lead the way. That meant figuring out what Copilot, and the future of work, should look like as one ecosystem. We still have a ways to go, but the progress over the past year has been inspiring to watch. A lot of talented people set aside their own roadmaps to make that happen. Thank you. I know it wasn’t easy. Satya, thank you. When LinkedIn joined Microsoft, you gave us room to build, and then trusted many of us with a lot more. I’ve learned more from you than I can fit in an email, and I’m grateful for the friendship that came with it. All of which made this a hard decision. I know what it would take for me to lead the next phase of this work well: being in Redmond full time, every day. But my life and my family’s life are here in the Bay Area. My wife Leigh gives her time to more local organizations than I can keep track of. Our youngest daughter just started high school, and our dog Buddy remains deeply committed to the trails on the Peninsula! I thought about this for a long time. It’s the right call. The work now goes to leaders who are set up to take it further. I can’t wait to see what they do with it. Over the years, people have asked me what’s kept me so energized and motivated in this work. I think the answer is that I got to spend my career working where doing good and doing well are the same thing. In technology, that’s the best place to operate. Most companies start by focusing on doing well, so doing good becomes a compromise. It’s the last slide of the PowerPoint, or a separate .org. Satya Nadella, Chairman and CEO, and Ryan Roslansky, Executive Vice President of LinkedIn and Microsoft 365, shared the below communications with Microsoft and LinkedIn employees this morning.

SATYA NADELLA MESSAGE

After nearly 18 years at LinkedIn and Microsoft, Ryan Roslansky has decided to leave Microsoft and embark on his next chapter.

As Ryan and I have been discussing our roadmap and work ahead, we felt this was the right moment for this change. Ryan will stay through the end of the calendar year as an advisor to me and will support on the transition.

Ryan leaves the organization in a strong position. With Copilot, we are executing rapidly against our vision to build a new OS for work that spans every model, every form factor, and every task, with Office fully embedded in Copilot and vice versa! Over the past year, Ryan’s team has done critical work bringing together the product, engineering, and design foundations that have made this next phase possible. Last week’s launch was an important milestone in that journey, and the strong response from customers, partners, and the broader ecosystem reinforced both how far we’ve come and how much opportunity remains ahead.

At LinkedIn, we remain focused on our core vision of creating economic opportunity for every member of the global workforce, helping our 1.3 billion members access the knowledge, insights, and opportunities they need to navigate rapidly changing professional and labor markets.

Effective today we will make the following changes:

  • Sumit Chauhan and Lan Ye will report to Charles Lamanna.
  • Jon Friedman will report to Jacob Andreou.
  • Dan Shapero will continue as CEO of LinkedIn and Mohak Shroff will continue in his role, both reporting to me.

Over his nearly two decades at Microsoft, Ryan has helped shape how people around the world find opportunity, build their careers, and get their work done. I’ve always appreciated his clarity of thinking and I’m deeply grateful for everything Ryan has built, for the leaders and teams he has developed, and for his friendship and counsel.

Please join me in thanking Ryan for his extraordinary contributions to LinkedIn and Microsoft, and in wishing him the very best in what comes next.

Satya

RYAN ROSLANSKY MESSAGE

Team,

In 1996, as a college freshman, I taught myself to code so a few friends and I could help other students find a place to live around campus. I didn’t know much. I did know the internet was about to change how people found things, and I wanted to be as close to that as possible.

In 2009, Jeff Weiner made me his first hire at LinkedIn. I’ve spent the nearly 18 years since working on a much bigger version of that same idea: helping people find opportunity, and then helping them do great work once they have it.

This has (obviously) been the best professional experience of my life.

As a product manager, I got to build dozens of features that are still around today (some good, some not so good!). When I became CEO in 2020, the world was months into a pandemic that changed what work even meant. Nobody hands you a playbook for that. This team wrote one anyway. Since then, LinkedIn has passed a billion members and nearly tripled its business, and every bit of that belongs to the people who built it.

Last year, Satya asked me to help build the future of M365. Once again, the old rules didn’t apply. AI was rapidly changing how professionals work, and the world’s largest productivity suite needed to lead the way. That meant figuring out what Copilot, and the future of work, should look like as one ecosystem.

We still have a ways to go, but the progress over the past year has been inspiring to watch. A lot of talented people set aside their own roadmaps to make that happen. Thank you. I know it wasn’t easy.

Satya, thank you. When LinkedIn joined Microsoft, you gave us room to build, and then trusted many of us with a lot more. I’ve learned more from you than I can fit in an email, and I’m grateful for the friendship that came with it.

All of which made this a hard decision. I know what it would take for me to lead the next phase of this work well: being in Redmond full time, every day. But my life and my family’s life are here in the Bay Area. My wife Leigh gives her time to more local organizations than I can keep track of. Our youngest daughter just started high school, and our dog Buddy remains deeply committed to the trails on the Peninsula!

I thought about this for a long time. It’s the right call. The work now goes to leaders who are set up to take it further. I can’t wait to see what they do with it.

Over the years, people have asked me what’s kept me so energized and motivated in this work. I think the answer is that I got to spend my career working where doing good and doing well are the same thing. In technology, that’s the best place to operate.

Most companies start by focusing on doing well, so doing good becomes a compromise. It’s the last slide of the PowerPoint, or a separate .org. And for our business too.

Not many companies get to work this way, and not many people get the chance to build something like it. We do.

That matters more now than it ever has. Technology will continue to touch every job on the planet, and the people building it will decide what kind of world it helps create. I can’t think of a better group to figure that out than the people reading this note.

Thank you for the best 18 years I could have asked for.

title: New Microsoft data innovations unlock what only your business knows
text: Every organization has knowledge that is uniquely its own: the way its business operates, the data it has built over time, the expertise of its people and the context behind thousands of everyday decisions. As powerful AI models become more widely available, that unique business intelligence matters more than ever. The difference will come from how effectively organizations combine those models with the data, expertise and business context that make them unique. Turning that intelligence into lasting advantage requires three elements to work together: human ambition to set the direction, intelligence grounded in the organization’s unique knowledge and trust to provide the foundation for operating at scale. Microsoft’s approach is designed to bring those elements together so organizations can build on what they know and create greater value over time. That value can compound through a continuous learning loop, where AI draws on an organization’s data and expertise, improves the systems and experiences it creates and generates better outcomes over time without making the organization dependent on any single model provider. Today at the European Microsoft Fabric + SQL Community Conference in Barcelona, we are introducing advances across Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databases that help organizations put their data estate at the heart of a successful AI strategy. Fabric IQ: Bring your unique business context into Microsoft Copilot As Microsoft Copilot evolves across Home, Code and Autopilot, access to trusted business context becomes essential. Fabric IQ brings governed business context into Copilot, grounding experiences in the Power BI semantic models, metrics, relationships and business definitions organizations already trust. With Fabric IQ in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Cowork now generally available, users can ask business questions and receive answers grounded in governed Power BI data, while Cowork can use those insights as part of broader multistep work. Integration with the new Code experience is coming through the Frontier program. That means when someone asks Copilot for the latest sales forecast or another critical business metric, the answer can be grounded in the same semantic model that powers the organization’s reports, helping avoid confusion about which number is correct. For Power BI customers, this extends the semantic foundation they already have into Microsoft Copilot while preserving existing access controls and governance. I experienced this myself recently as I was preparing for a sales review and asked Copilot, “What’s our latest sales forecast?” With Fabric IQ, that answer was grounded in the same governed Power BI semantic model that powers the team’s sales reporting, using the same business definitions and metrics my team already trusts. So, instead of spending the meeting uncovering and debating whose number was right, the team was able to get straight to what the numbers mean and focus on what we do next. That’s exactly the kind of experience we want to create. For Fabric and Power BI customers, this capability is on by default in Copilot Chat and Cowork and extends the semantic foundation they already have into Microsoft Copilot while preserving existing access controls and governance. IQ Sharing in Microsoft Fabric: Share unique business context without giving up control Business knowledge does not stop at the boundary of a team or business unit. Organizations increasingly need to collaborate across customers, partners and broader ecosystems while maintaining control over the information they share. IQ Sharing in Fabric, now in preview as part of Fabric IQ, breaks down company boundaries by enabling organizations to securely share data and the business context that gives it meaning, while maintaining governance over the underlying assets. Starting with key Fabric IQ artifacts and context, IQ Share is designed to evolve beyond preview to help customers discover, share and activate trusted context wherever it’s needed. Together with OneLake mirroring and shortcuts, these investments create a more open foundation for sharing governed data and context across organizations, platforms and ecosystems. Observability in Microsoft Fabric: Maintain visibility and control as AI scales As organizations put more workloads on their unified data platform, they need to understand system health and address issues before they affect business and AI outcomes. Observability in Fabric helps teams move from reactive troubleshooting to proactive operations. Cross-workspace monitoring and an enhanced Monitor Hub provide a unified view across jobs, capacities, workspaces and workloads, while Operations Agents and Activator help teams investigate issues, identify root causes with AI and automate responses. Together, these capabilities help organizations maintain oversight as they scale data and AI. Fabric Apps: Build applications directly on governed business data AI is transforming how applications are created, but enterprises still need a secure, governed path from idea to production. Fabric Apps brings application development directly to governed data in Microsoft Fabric, helping organizations build and scale AI-powered business applications faster. With new capabilities for data connectivity, transactional workloads, backend logic, storage and policy-controlled access, developers can move from prototype to production on a unified data foundation. These experiences bring application creation closer to where enterprise data and insights already live, helping more people turn data into action. Agentic data engineering: Automate the work, stay in control A continuous learning loop is only as good as the data behind it, which must be prepared, refined and improved without pause. As those environments become more complex, organizations need automation that can take on more of that work without pushing people or controls out of the loop. Earlier this year, we shared our vision for autonomous data engineering . Now, new agentic data engineering features in Fabric bring that vision to life, bringing autonomous execution to complex data engineering initiatives while keeping organizations in control. Engineers define the outcome and set the boundaries. Inside those limits, the agent plans and executes the work, validates the results and refines the approach. SQL Server on Azure Local: Keep critical data and workloads where you need them Maintaining control over business knowledge also means having flexibility over where critical data and workloads run. Now generally available, SQL Server on Azure Local brings SQL Server and Azure services into local environments, giving organizations more choice to run workloads closer to their applications and operations. SQL Server on Azure Local with disconnected operations, now in preview, extends that flexibility to environments where cloud connectivity is interrupted, restricted or unavailable. These options give organizations operating across regulated, local, edge and disconnected environments greater choice over where their critical data and workloads reside and operate. Database Hub in Fabric: Simplify database management with agentic assistance Intelligent applications depend on operational data. Teams need a clear view of the databases that power those applications and practical tools to manage them. Building on its introduction at FabCon Atlanta, Database Hub in Fabric is now in public preview. It provides a central control plane for managing SQL Server, Azure SQL, PostgreSQL, Cosmos DB and SQL databases in Fabric, helping administrators monitor and govern their database estate. Complementing this management experience, specialist database agents for SQL and PostgreSQL in Database Hub in Fabric and Visual Studio Code, coming soon to public preview, help teams investigate issues, understand performance bottlenecks and identify optimization opportunities within their development environment. Together, these capabilities help teams understand their database estate and make more informed operational decisions. Build AI on the knowledge that makes your business different Our goal is straightforward: help organizations use the best AI models and tools available while turning their proprietary data, expertise and workflows into an advantage that grows more valuable over time. That direction is reflected across today’s announcements as the data foundation comes into focus. At Ignite , we’ll broaden this story across the full Microsoft Frontier ecosystem, connecting data, applications, agents, governance and infrastructure into one system that turns AI ambition into business outcomes. Explore the complete set of announcements across Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databases in today’s blog from Arun Ulagaratchagan, Executive Vice President of Azure Data. Jessica Hawk leads Azure Product Marketing at Microsoft, driving strategy and storytelling across the full Azure portfolio. Her team defines how Azure shows up in the market — helping customers and developers tap into the platform’s full potential across cloud, data, AI and developer innovation. title: Introducing the new Copilot with Home, Code and Autopilot
text: We’re reimagining Microsoft Copilot to enable work as it evolves and to help expand what every individual and every organization can accomplish in the flow of human ambition. Today we’re introducing the new Copilot to connect the tools people rely on with the next generation of capabilities they’ll need to build, customize and scale AI across work. The Copilot app now has three new capabilities: Home is your new starting point, where Chat and Cowork come together — and with Office in Copilot , the full power of Word, Excel and PowerPoint is now built into the experience. Code lets everyone build their own solutions with the tools to run them safely, and it’s powered by the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot. And Autopilot is a persistent, proactive and personal agent that keeps working even when you’re not. Home and Code will start rolling out in our Frontier program in the coming weeks and Autopilot is expanding to private preview at the end of the month. We’re also excited to share new FinOps for AI capabilities to help you manage spend and get the most value from Copilot and agents. YouTube Video Click here to load media Watch the audio-described version . A new experience for every mode of work Home is your new starting point in Copilot, where Chat and Cowork come together in one place. As work moves constantly between meetings, chats, documents, emails, apps and agents, Home is where you get your bearings, keeping you grounded and moving forward. You can review recent activity, get suggestions on what Copilot can help with, and pick up work right where you left off. Chat is instant and conversational — ready for quick questions, lookups, draft-creation and keeping you in the loop on every turn. Cowork is for work you delegate. You define the task and it runs end-to-end to return a completed result: an RFP response, a launch kit, a customer briefing, a financial close package or any other complex work worth iterating on. And coming soon, you won’t need to choose a mode: simply state what you need to accomplish, and Copilot will route the work to Chat, Cowork or Code — whichever capability is right for the job. We’re also bringing the full power of Word, Excel and PowerPoint to Copilot with Office in Copilot . Now you can get to real work fast: no broken formatting, no stray versions, no rebuilding the context in another app. From Home you can ask Copilot to draft a launch brief, model a budget, build a deck, or pick up a file your team is already working on, and it creates or updates a real, editable document, workbook or presentation — live for your whole team, not just you. Refine it side by side with your conversation, or @mention a teammate and their edits show up as they make them — things stay in sync between Copilot and the Office apps, so progress travels with you wherever you work. If you haven’t used Copilot in the Office apps lately, take another look. PowerPoint now keeps decks on-brand automatically and enables you to fine-tune slides and images or quickly apply a custom template. When Copilot or another collaborator makes edits in Excel, you can see exactly what changed and why, so you’re up to speed quickly, and Copilot recommends the best chart to visualize your data. And across Microsoft 365, Skills help bring specialized expertise directly into the apps, like financial skills in Excel and legal skills in Word, and enable organizations to scale best practices through reusable, role-specific workflows. Code moves solution-building outside the realm of developers alone. To date, the unit of knowledge work has been the file: the document, the spreadsheet, the deck. Those aren’t going anywhere, but Code adds a fourth: small, purpose-built solutions anyone can create to get a job done. Learning to build them is becoming as basic a skill as writing a memo or modeling a budget. Describe an app, tracker, dashboard, automation or workflow in natural language, and Copilot chooses an approach and builds it — from persistent desktop widgets for quick reference and interactive dashboards for exploring data and testing outcomes to cloud-hosted internal apps you can share with your team. Powered by the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot, Code runs in a sandboxed environment and can be hosted securely within your tenant. With Microsoft IQ, everything you create is grounded in the context of your work, and plugins sync automatically. Your software developers continue to use GitHub Copilot for their day-to-day work with more connectivity into the Copilot platform. Code is rolling out to Frontier at the end of the month, with broad availability in the coming weeks. It will be in preview for Microsoft 365 Premium and Pro subscribers later this year. As it gets easier and faster than ever to build in Copilot, we’re introducing Microsoft Copilot Managed Runtime : hosting infrastructure that lets code run safely right inside your company’s Microsoft 365 environment. It’s governed by IT but easy for everyone else: share an app with teammates, connect it to live data and access it from anywhere. This same foundation enables apps built in Cowork, Code and Copilot Studio, and we’re opening it up to third-party and pro-code developers, too. Copilot Managed Runtime is now in preview and will also be accessible inside Code. Autopilot , previously called Scout, is your digital teammate. And it works for you: Give it a name, a role and a goal, and it goes to work — watching channels, following up on threads, running recurring work and picking a project back up days later, without waiting for a prompt. It can do things like set up and manage a full supplier review process: building the schedule and workback plan, then handling prep, meetings and follow-ups on its own, right down to reaching out to stakeholders for updates. And Autopilot is cloud-hosted, so it keeps working while you sleep or your attention is elsewhere — no constant monitoring required. Autopilot lives in your tenant with its own identity, memory, computer and workspace, and it’s built on Microsoft IQ so it understands how your organization actually works. It shows up where people already work — Teams, Outlook, chats, channels and documents — so you can @mention it like a colleague, with permissions, audit and governance behind it. You set the objective and boundaries; Autopilot handles the rest while keeping you informed and in control. Expanding your business context Copilot is grounded in Microsoft IQ, the unified intelligence platform for enterprise AI across your Microsoft stack, connecting how the business operates with the knowledge it holds into one real-time view for Copilot and your agents, governed and secure. Today we are expanding the business context available to Copilot. Fabric IQ brings trusted context from your data, including the 20+ million semantic models in Power BI into Copilot. It grounds Chat and Cowork, and is generally available in both today, with Code integration coming through the Frontier program soon. Rolling out over the next month in public preview, Copilot is now grounded in data and workflows from Dynamics 365 and Power Platform. So, when a salesperson is working on a proposal, for instance, Copilot can incorporate data like deal history and support tickets right into the document, with no app-switching or distracting lookups required. You also need a trusted way to connect Copilot to the actions and data that move your business forward. Plugins extend what Copilot can do, bringing together skills, connectors and other capabilities so users can complete more workflows without leaving the apps they use every day. Rolling out now and generally available across surfaces in the coming weeks, a new plugin registry will bring Microsoft, partner and custom-built plugins together in one unified catalog. IT can approve and manage plugins centrally, while developers and partners can publish once to extend Copilot across supported experiences. The result is a simpler way to introduce trusted capabilities at scale, with the control your organization needs. Managing AI spend For everyday AI — quick answers, first drafts, summaries and analysis — you want the best possible quality at a fixed cost. A user subscription license (USL) gives you exactly that: Copilot in Chat and across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams; model selection; and new capabilities and models. Auto is at the heart of the USL. Auto weighs accuracy, speed and cost on each request to route to the model best suited for the job. Agentic work requires a different type of spend, one that gives you the best quality possible with the most advanced models. Usage-based billing (UBB) lets you have full control to choose models and match cost to value. Cowork, Code, and Autopilot, new long-running agentic capabilities, and frontier models like Astra and Fable all run on UBB. As AI capabilities and the ways people use them continue to evolve, we’re evolving Copilot pricing alongside them. Read more here . FinOps for AI is a shared discipline for managing AI spend and optimizing it for business value. We are committed to enabling organizations to make the most of their AI spend, and, today, we are introducing new capabilities across Agent 365, Insights and Microsoft Copilot to help do that. Cost management in Agent 365 is expanding beyond Cowork and Work IQ APIs to include Code and Copilot Managed Runtime, with support for agents built in Microsoft Copilot Studio planned for October. Admins can manage spending policies at scale with API access; route credit requests from end users into existing approval and automation workflows; and set which model families are available to different groups of users — those settings also shape which models Auto can select from. Business leaders and admins can understand which Cowork tasks are generating the strongest outcomes and determine where to sustain, expand or optimize usage. And finally, end users can view credit usage, remaining balances and usage history directly in Microsoft Copilot, so they can better manage their own AI usage within organizational guardrails. We are committed to investing in FinOps for AI to help organizations stay in control of spend, understand value and optimize their AI investments for impact. A sneak peek at what’s next These announcements are just the beginning. We’re excited to share future Copilot experiences that make Copilot more personalized and proactive, and help the team move forward together. Coming soon in Home, Today is a proactive, personalized command center across mail, calendar, Teams threads, meetings and tasks. It shows you what you missed, what needs attention now and what can wait. Today doesn’t just surface the work, it gets work done. The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly. Today enters private preview in October in Copilot, and will be coming to Outlook and Teams as well. YouTube Video Click here to load media Watch the audio-described version . And now when you invoke @Copilot in Teams , your entire team gets the shared context and permissions of the channel, group chat or meeting. Ask why a product decision was made, and Copilot pulls the background from across conversations — no digging, no re-explaining. When that decision ripples into manufacturing, packaging and launch timing, Copilot goes further: it offers to prepare a cross-functional review with dependencies, owners, open questions and decisions, so everyone can see how their work connects and what still needs resolving. The team stays aligned and the project keeps moving forward. The @Copilot capability will be in private preview in Teams by the end of the month. YouTube Video Click here to load media Watch the audio-described version . Get started With the new Copilot, you now have one place to ask, delegate, build, automate and more. It’s rolling out now through the Frontier program , with new capabilities arriving continuously. Check back here for the latest. There is so much more coming to Copilot. Join us at Microsoft Ignite — November 17–20 in San Francisco and online — to learn about the latest Copilot innovation and how it’s empowering people and organizations to reimagine work and get value from AI. Jared Spataro leads Microsoft’s AI at Work efforts, helping every organization leverage AI and agents to solve their unique business problems, reduce costs and drive net-new value creation. His team conducts research to help predict and shape what the future of work and business will look like across industries, while also delivering new products and features within Copilot, Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and Power Platform.
