  • 94% monthly adoption and 85% weekly usage
  • 63% of enabled employees using Copilot three or more days per week
  • 81% of employees reporting time savings, with 84% redirecting that time to higher-value work and 73% improving quality of output

The impact goes beyond individual productivity into agentic AI in core business operations:

  • Finance operations modernized with intelligent agents, driving 95% faster lead times and more than 37% reduction in operational costs
  • A multi-agent AI framework was deployed across 130,000 Assurance professionals and 160,000 audit engagements
  • Tax workflows were transformed through document automation, reducing manual effort by up to 90%

With these results, EY is now expanding Copilot through Microsoft 365 E7 to more than 400,000 of its people worldwide, moving from early success to true enterprise scale.

It’s also why EY serves as Customer Zero — applying Microsoft AI technologies internally to prove what works before bringing those solutions to clients.

But what differentiates this initiative isn’t just what we bring. It’s how we deliver it.

At its core is a shared focus on helping organizations become Frontier Firms — where AI is embedded across the enterprise, not layered on top.

In a Frontier Firm, data, workflows and decision-making are connected end to end. AI becomes part of how work happens, and human expertise is amplified by intelligent systems.

Reaching this level requires more than investment. It requires execution.

A new model for execution at scale

This is where our approach is fundamentally different.

Microsoft and EY are cooperating as an integrated transformation engine — co-developing, co-engineering and co-delivering solutions aligned to real business priorities.

A key part of this model is Microsoft’s Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), who work side by side with EY transformation teams directly within customer environments.

Together, these teams:

  • Co-create solutions grounded in business needs
  • Accelerate deployment across complex systems
  • Stay engaged from initial use case through full-scale adoption

This integrated model closes the gap between strategy and execution. It reduces friction across the technology stack and creates a direct path from pilot to production — at enterprise scale.
It also ensures that intelligence and trust advance together, embedding AI across data, applications and infrastructure in ways that can be governed, secured and continuously optimized.

Importantly, it establishes a repeatable blueprint — one that organizations can use to scale AI adoption across functions, industries and geographies.

Why this matters now

Organizations are under pressure to move faster — to go beyond experimentation and deliver AI across the enterprise.

What they need is not just technology, but a clear path to execution — grounded in both intelligence and trust.

AI is not simply about doing work faster. It’s about enabling people and organizations to do more — focusing on insight, creativity and higher-value decision-making.

Our work with EY demonstrates what’s possible when AI is deployed with purpose at scale. Together, we are bringing those learnings to customers around the world — helping them accelerate transformation, unlock efficiencies and create new opportunities for growth.

Microsoft and EY are committed to helping organizations turn AI ambition into enterprise impact.

Learn more in the official announcement.

title: How Frontier Firms are rebuilding the operating model for the age of AI
text: Updated May 11, 2026: The post was updated to reflect that third-party plugins will be available starting May 12, 2026. Spend time with any software engineering team right now and you’ll see something worth paying attention to. Over the last few years, the way software gets built has moved through four distinct patterns of human-agent collaboration — and the same patterns are beginning to show up across other functions of the firm. Author: You’re producing the work, calling on AI to help as needed — a line of code, a sentence, a chart. Editor: You set the intent and AI creates the first draft for you to edit and approve. Director: You create a spec and hand off entire tasks for AI to execute in the background. Orchestrator: You design a system where multiple agents run in parallel across a workflow, flagging exceptions and escalations to you. Every business leader knows the world is changing, but far fewer have a clear picture of what to do about it. These four patterns are the place to start. The real work ahead for leaders is redesigning their firm’s operating model around the collaboration patterns. As agent use increases, human involvement doesn’t disappear — it changes shape. What declines is the amount of tactical, step-by-step execution work humans do themselves. And what rises is the need for humans to set direction, define standards and evaluate outcomes. Ultimately, the goal is not to move every task and business process to the fourth pattern. Instead, it’s up to leaders to help their organizations develop clarity around matching workstreams to the right collaboration pattern. That’s the shape of the Frontier Firm: defined by how deliberately leaders design work across functions, matching the level of human involvement to the outcome. What the data shows Our 2026 Work Trend Index research reinforces this shift across roles and industries. We analyzed trillions of anonymized Microsoft 365 productivity signals and surveyed 20,000 workers using AI across 10 countries. We also spoke with leading experts in AI, work and organizational psychology to help us unpack the insights from the data and understand where all this is going. The conclusion is consistent: the constraint is no longer what people can do, it is how work is structured around them. AI lifts individual potential. A privacy-preserving analysis of more than 100,000 chats in Microsoft 365 Copilot shows that 49% of all conversations support cognitive work — helping workers analyze information, solve problems, evaluate and think creatively. This shift is already visible in output, with 58% of AI users saying they’re producing work they couldn’t have a year ago, rising to 80% among Frontier Professionals , the most advanced AI users in our research. Additionally, when AI users were asked which human skills are most important as AI takes on more work, they said two topped the list: quality control of AI output (50%) and critical thinking — that is, analyzing information objectively and making a reasoned judgment (46%). The Transformation Paradox. We are seeing a pressure point emerge within the organization where the pull to perform collides with the push to transform. 65% of AI users surveyed fear falling behind if they don’t use AI to adapt quickly, yet 45% say it feels safer to focus on current goals than to redesign work with AI. And only 13% of workers say they’re rewarded for reinvention of work with AI even if results aren’t met. The same forces accelerating AI adoption are holding it back. Every organization is a learning system. Our results show that organizational factors like culture, manager support and talent practices account for more than 2X the AI impact of individual factors like mindset and behavior (67% vs. 32%). Specifically, the findings underscore the importance of an AI-ready environment: a culture that treats AI as a strategic advantage and encourages experimentation, managers who model and incentivize AI use and talent practices that build skills and create space to apply them. The real question isn’t whether people have the right skills, it’s whether the organization is built to unlock them. The firms that build a new operating model today won’t just move faster in the short term. They’ll build something more durable, setting themselves up to create value in ways that we can’t yet conceive of: an organization that learns faster than its competitors, compounds its own intelligence and gets harder to catch with every cycle. For deeper analysis, see the 2026 Work Trend Index Report . Enabling the Frontier Firm with Copilot Cowork — now mobile, extensible and enterprise-ready None of an organization’s system scales without infrastructure that brings people and agents into the same flow of work with connected data and the ability to manage and govern it all. Microsoft 365 Copilot is built for exactly that. Today, we’re expanding Copilot Cowork with new capabilities for Frontier customers to help organizations move from isolated AI tasks to coordinated, multistep work. Cowork enables people to define outcomes and delegate work across apps, business systems and data, with execution that stays directed and controlled throughout. This update introduces Copilot Cowork Mobile for iOS and Android , along with a growing plugin ecosystem for Cowork, bringing more of an organization’s tools and data into these experiences. This includes native plugins across Microsoft services like Dynamics 365 and Fabric, and partner integrations available in the coming weeks like LSEG (London Stock Exchange Group), Miro, monday.com, S&P Global Energy and more. Organizations can also build custom plugins to turn their own workflows and expertise into reusable, scalable processes. Additionally, a first wave of federated Copilot connectors in Researcher and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is generally available today from partners like HubSpot, LSEG (London Stock Exchange Group), Moody’s, Notion and more. Together, these updates extend Copilot Cowork from a task-based assistant into an extensible platform that helps orchestrate work across Microsoft and third-party systems. With management and governance through Microsoft Agent 365, organizations can deploy and scale agents across core business functions like sales, service and operations. For more on these product innovations: Microsoft 365 blog . AI is no longer an experiment. It is an execution challenge. Employees are already working across all four patterns. The open question for every leadership team is whether they can catch up. Access to AI won’t be the advantage for much longer. How the work is designed around it will be. Jared Spataro, CMO, AI at Work at Microsoft, shapes how every organization applies AI and agents to reduce costs, create new value and define the future of work. He leads research, strategy and product across Copilot, Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and Power Platform. title: Unlocking human ambition to drive business growth with AI
text: As our customers progress toward becoming Frontier Firms, they are using AI not only to optimize how work gets done, but to reinvent their business on the promise of growth. Organizations can now unlock creativity, accelerate innovation and democratize intelligence by bringing Copilots and agents directly into the tools people love and use every day. As adoption continues to scale, business value is no longer measured solely by time saved or productivity gained, but in how effectively organizations translate their unique IQ into decisions that drive measurable impact across core business processes. The two most important elements in any AI solution are Intelligence + Trust. At Microsoft, we are focused on providing a platform for both through Microsoft IQ and Agent 365, respectively, so customers can harness the power of AI, have it amplify their unique differentiation and do so in a model diverse, open and heterogeneous manner. Microsoft IQ brings context to your data and provides faster, more accurate, more trusted experiences across modalities of chat, artifact creation and augmentation, and agent development; all while safeguarding your assets and protecting your intellectual property. Agent 365 provides observability, governance and security across all the agents you build — whether on Microsoft’s platform or third-party environments — so you can trust the outcomes you achieve with AI and ensure ROI for the same. With intelligence embedded into daily work, organizations are activating human ambition — engaging customers more effectively, reshaping business processes and accelerating innovation without adding operational complexity — turning gains into competitive advantage. Trust makes this durable, allowing organizations to scale securely with AI. The shift to becoming Frontier can be seen in our recent partnerships, with BMW Group selecting Microsoft for its large-scale deployment of Microsoft 365 Copilot across its global workforce and Accenture rolling out Copilot to more than 740,000 employees. Frontier Transformation — built on a foundation of Intelligence + Trust — is how organizations are enabling AI for growth; moving from aspiration to outcome with confidence, driving measurable business gains and maintaining the rigor required to operate AI responsibly. Across industries, our customers and partners are putting AI to work to reveal new sources of innovation and business value. I am pleased to highlight additional stories from this past quarter. With millions of customer queries overwhelming its support channels, Air India was facing rising costs, slower response times and growing frustration for customers and employees. Within six months, internal development teams built an agentic AI solution using Azure OpenAI and in Foundry models. AI.g handles 40,000 customer queries daily and since launching has saved the company millions of dollars . The agent has resolved more than 13 million conversations with a 97% success rate, allowing employees to focus on contributing at a higher level — solving complex cases that require nuanced human judgement and problem-solving skills. Air India is the first airline worldwide to deploy generative AI for customer service at scale. As the second largest school district in Florida, Broward County Public Schools serve approximately 235,000 students across 235 schools and 25,000 employees. Although the district had extensive data, it lacked the real-time insights required to support its students — while simultaneously facing a $90-million budget shortfall. Rather than slowing innovation, the district used financial pressure as a catalyst to modernize systems and rethink how work was done. By deploying Microsoft 365 Copilot, educators and staff reclaimed six to seven hours weekly — time redirected to students for direct interaction, coaching and feedback . The district also equipped students with Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Copilot Studio to provide faster access to learning resources and foster more equitable learning — providing support for students with disabilities, English language learners and those needing additional academic assistance. The district’s adoption of Copilot — the largest K-12 deployment globally — is also expected to generate $40 to $50 million in savings over five years. Cemex is one of the world’s largest building materials companies, operating more than 50 cement plants and over 1,000 ready mix plants across four continents. To accelerate execution at scale, Cemex built LUCA Bot — an AI agent built in Microsoft Foundry with Azure OpenAI — giving approximately 100 senior business leaders visibility into company-wide performance across more than 120 KPIs. The self-service tool processes 400 to 500 queries per month with high accuracy , delivering real-time, conversational insights across global sales, plant operations and financial performance. By compressing decision cycles from days to seconds , the company shifted from reactive to real-time decision-making — allowing leaders to recognize demand signals faster, improve operational efficiency and drive business outcomes across its multi-billion-dollar enterprise. Cybersecurity startup ContraForce is democratizing enterprise-grade protection for managed service providers by operationalizing Microsoft’s security — Microsoft Sentinel, Defender XDR, Entra ID and Azure OpenAI in Foundry models — into a turnkey, AI-driven platform. Built for environments where traditional tools were too complex and costly for most providers to operate efficiently, the solution automates more than 90% of incident response, reducing cost per incident and enabling 24/7 protection . Providers can onboard more customers, deliver higher-quality security services and scale operations without adding headcount — transforming security delivery into a growth engine. Analysts can manage significantly more volume with incidents resolving in minutes and teams freed to focus on more strategic advisory work . As global professional services firm KPMG expanded its Digital Gateway platform to support secure, global engagement with clients and professionals, its data environment grew increasingly fragmented and complex — spanning multiple tools and systems that slowed collaboration and increased operational effort. The company established Microsoft Fabric as its strategic data platform; unifying its data engineering, storage, analytics, reporting and global security policies into a single, trusted environment and pacing adoption as it matured in enterprise governance. Client data onboarding times were 87% faster — from sixteen hours to two — and operational IT efforts were reduced by 25% . With a governed, real-time data foundation, KPMG is accelerating insights; enabling faster, more confident decisions and freeing teams to provide consistent, high-quality client value delivery across global engagements . To democratize AI across its digital workplace, Mercedes-Benz is deploying Microsoft 365 Copilot company-wide — one of the largest, most comprehensive industry deployments in European industry. Moving beyond selective use of AI, the company is integrating it systematically into day-to-day work, supporting decision-making and core operational processes while reducing complexity. By placing secure, enterprise-grade AI in the hands of employees across functions, Mercedes-Benz is enabling faster execution, lowering operating costs and driving more consistent performance across its global business . Copilot is also helping teams strengthen decision quality at scale , enabling them to respond more precisely and compete more effectively in dynamic markets. As one of the world’s busiest rail operators, MTR manages high‑volume, complex transit operations with strict service and reliability expectations. To simplify complex administrative workloads and accelerate decision‑making, MTR deployed Microsoft 365 Copilot alongside Power Platform, embedding role‑based copilots and low‑code workflows across drafting, summarization and analysis. The result reduced manual effort, shortened turnaround times and improved operational consistency across its network . To improve passenger services, the company also launched AI Tracy — a personalized assistant built on Microsoft Azure that provides real-time guidance on ticketing, station facilities and local amenities. With AI embedded into everyday workflows and passenger services, MTR is extending consistent, real-time service across its network and expanding what teams can achieve and execute with AI . PepsiCo operates one of the world’s largest consumer goods enterprises, with 320,000 employees across more than 200 countries. The company faced a fragmented technology landscape, with disparate collaboration and tools that slowed coordination. This limited PepsiCo’s ability to grow its business, so the company standardized on Microsoft Teams and deployed Microsoft 365 Copilot to create a unified, secure foundation to innovate with AI. With Teams and Copilot seamlessly embedded into the tools employees use every day, PepsiCo is improving how work gets done. With 90% to 95% daily Copilot usage , AI is embedded in everyday work — creating a more connected environment that fosters collaboration and reduces friction, saving employees hours each day and freeing up time for them to focus on higher-impact work . Global real estate developer Tata Realty manages a diverse portfolio spanning residential, commercial, mixed-use and infrastructure in Southeast Asia. As the business grew, fragmented data across finance, operations, engineering, safety and HR made it difficult to generate insights — slowing decision-making, increasing costs and introducing operational risk. By adopting Microsoft Fabric as a unified, governed data platform, the company consolidated engineering, warehousing and reporting into a single environment. This move helped reduce data processing time by 20% and lower annual analytics costs by 20% to 30% . With real-time, cross-functional insights now embedded in core workflows, teams are making faster, more informed decisions and operating with greater speed, consistency and control across the business . Tru Cooperative Bank (formerly First West Credit Union) serves more than 250,000 members with complex financial products and high service expectations. By deploying Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio, the organization reduced administrative effort and accelerated service delivery, reaching 93% employee adoption and 90% weekly usage . With AI embedded in daily workflows, employees can instantly access and bring together member context, policies and procedures — enabling faster decision cycles and more proactive, personalized guidance . By automating routine work, teams are creating space to focus on higher-value client conversations that deepen relationships, advance financial outcomes and drive member growth — with human ambition at the center of every interaction . At the same time, moving from reactive work to real-time, insight-driven engagement is strengthening member trust and scaling consistent, high-quality delivery across the organization . Frontier Transformation is changing how organizations operate, compete and grow. By embedding intelligence into the flow of work and grounding it in enterprise‑grade trust, businesses are operating with greater precision and expanding what their teams can achieve at global scale. With an open, model-diverse and secure platform, Microsoft enables organizations to unlock human ambition and leverage AI for growth — transforming their unique IQ into decisions and actions that drive measurable business outcomes. We are grateful for the continued trust of our customers and partners. Together, we are shaping how every organization can lead with AI. Judson Althoff is the chief executive officer of the commercial business at Microsoft. He is responsible for the product strategy, sales, services, support, marketing, operations and revenue growth of the company’s commercial business, which operates in more than 120 regional and national subsidiaries globally. title: Microsoft Sovereign Private Cloud scales to thousands of nodes with Azure Local
text: Today, I am pleased to announce that Azure Local now scales to support deployments of up to thousands of servers within a single sovereign environment, allowing organizations to run much larger workloads locally across large-footprint datacenters, industrial environments and edge locations while maintaining control within their sovereign boundary. Organizations operating national infrastructure, regulated workloads or mission-critical services are navigating a fundamental shift in how cloud infrastructure must be deployed and managed. As digital sovereignty postures evolve and regulatory requirements tighten across regions, infrastructure strategies are increasingly shaped by the need to maintain jurisdictional control over data, operations and dependencies. At the same time, AI and data-intensive applications are moving closer to where data is generated, requiring infrastructure that can scale to support larger deployment footprints while maintaining operational control, compliance and data residency requirements within sovereign environments. Azure Local is the foundation for Microsoft’s Sovereign Private Cloud, allowing organizations to run cloud-consistent infrastructure on hardware they own and operate within their sovereign boundary. It supports deployments across connected, intermittently connected or fully disconnected environments. With Azure Local disconnected operations, customers retain the ability to apply policy enforcement, role-based access control, auditing and compliance configuration locally, allowing them control over how infrastructure is configured, secured and updated regardless of public cloud connectivity. Scaling Sovereign Private Cloud Sovereign Private Cloud deployments must scale to support not only larger workloads, but also the operational requirements of national infrastructure and regulated industries. Azure Local allows organizations to grow deployments from hundreds up to thousands of servers within a single sovereign boundary, allowing infrastructure to expand alongside demand without requiring architectural redesign. As deployment footprints grow, resiliency becomes essential to maintaining continuous operations for mission critical services. Expanded fault domains and infrastructure pools help prevent hardware failures from resulting in service outages, ensuring critical workloads remain operational across environments with varying levels of cloud connectivity. At these larger scale points, organizations can run data-intensive AI inference and analytics workloads entirely within their own environment. With support for high-performance graphics processing unit (GPU) infrastructure, sensitive models and operational data remain within customer-controlled infrastructure, while access management, auditing and compliance controls are maintained within the sovereign deployment. Built for challenging workloads Increased deployment scale unlocks new workload placement opportunities, from large sovereign private cloud deployments to distributed AI workloads, allowing organizations to run more data intensive and latency sensitive applications entirely within their sovereign boundary. AT&T, one of the world’s largest telecommunications operators, is deploying Azure Local to run mission-critical infrastructure on hardware they own in their environment. The goal: full operational control while running at the scale the business demands. “Azure Local provides the infrastructure foundation we need to run critical operations at scale, while ensuring control and governance across our environment. The consistency of the Azure operating model, delivered on our own infrastructure, is key as we continue to modernize while delivering reliable services to our customers.” — Sherry McCaughan, Vice President – Mobility Core Services, AT&T Kadaster, the Netherlands’ official land registry and mapping agency, is running Azure Local to keep sovereign control over some of the country’s most sensitive public data. “As a government agency responsible for some of the Netherlands’ most sensitive data, we need infrastructure that gives us full control over where our data lives and how it’s governed. Azure Local has been a consistent foundation for that — and as our workloads grow in scale and complexity, the platform has grown with us.” — Maarten van der Tol, General Manager, Kadaster FiberCop, Italy’s most advanced and extensive digital network operator is deploying Azure Local across its edge locations to bring sovereign cloud and AI services to organizations throughout the country. Fabio Veronese, Chief Information & Technology Officer commented: “FiberCop is better positioned than any other player on the Italian market to drive innovation and deliver cloud as well as AI services at national scale. Azure Local supports our mission to drive Italy’s digital future and brings Microsoft’s cloud capabilities to edge workloads across the country while keeping data sovereignty and compliance where they matter most.” The infrastructure behind Sovereign Private Cloud Azure Local is available today with validated compute and enterprise storage platforms from partners including DataON, Dell Technologies, Everpure, Hitachi Vantara, HPE, Lenovo and NetApp, allowing organizations to integrate existing Storage Area Networks (SAN) and preserve prior investments while allowing compute and storage resources to scale independently within their sovereign environment. At the silicon level, Intel® Xeon® 6 processors provide the compute foundation for the platform. Built for the density and performance demands of modern enterprise workloads, Xeon 6 also brings built-in AI acceleration with Intel® AMX, meaning organizations running inference or generative AI workloads within their sovereign environment do not need to introduce separate, specialized infrastructure to do so. Together, Azure Local, validated compute and enterprise storage platforms, accelerated computing platforms and underlying silicon can provide a datacenter-scale stack that supports sovereign infrastructure deployments while helping ensure data, models and execution remain within customer-controlled environments. Sovereign infrastructure built for your requirements Azure Local was built to meet customers where their requirements are whether that means strict data residency, disconnected operations, regulated workloads or AI running close to where data is generated. As these requirements evolve across regulated industries and governments worldwide, Sovereign Private Cloud deployments can expand from a single node at the edge to large enterprise-scale datacenter environments, running on hardware organizations own and operate, with consistent lifecycle management through Azure. title: Samsung Announces December Release for Intelligent Eyewear, Bringing a Smarter Way To See the World
text: Samsung Electronics today announced the upcoming launch of the full lineup of intelligent eyewear, delivering a smarter way to see the world through intuitive, hands-free AI assistance . Set for release in the U.S. and South Korea on Dec. 10 with pre-orders beginning today, the collection combines Samsung’s mobile engineering expertise with 30 distinctive designs 1 from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker for comfortable, stylish everyday wear. Developed in collaboration with Google and with Gemini built in, the intelligent eyewear helps users understand the world around them, communicate across languages and stay connected while remaining present in the moment. Responsibly designed with everyone’s comfort in mind, the intelligent eyewear has controls that put the user in charge and has privacy protections for both the wearer and people around them. Designed for Style and Everyday Comfort Gentle Monster and Warby Parker bring their design identities to a combined lineup of 30 designs, offering customers a wide range of frame shapes, colors, sizes, and lens treatments to match their personal style. Gentle Monster brings bold, disruptive aesthetics, while Warby Parker offers timeless designs with a refined appeal. ▲ The six frame designs of Gentle Monster Intelligent Eyewear with various colorways ▲ The three frame designs of Warby Parker Intelligent Eyewear in optical and sun versions Samsung’s engineering expertise brings together the advanced hardware required for intelligent eyewear in slim, lightweight frames without sacrificing durability or comfort. title: Finding the Perfect TV: A Guide to Samsung TVs
text: Choosing the right TV is a long-term decision that involves several factors — including screen size, picture quality, brightness, viewing environment, and preferred content. Advances in TV technology have expanded the options available, from OLED, QLED, and Neo QLED to the latest Micro RGB. AI capabilities now go beyond picture and sound optimization to support content discovery, device connectivity, and personalized viewing experiences. As a result, consumers are asking more specific questions about screen size, AI features, and their viewing needs rather than simply “Which TV is the best?” Samsung Newsroom outlines key criteria and answers common questions about buying a TV. How To Choose the Right TV Size When choosing a TV size, viewing distance and available space are key considerations. For comfortable, immersive viewing, the recommended distance is approximately 1.2 times the screen size in centimeters, based on a 40-degree field of view. 1 ▲ Recommended viewing distance by TV screen size For typical living room seating arrangements, recommended screen sizes vary by viewing distance: 1.5 to 2.0 meters: 43- to 55-inch TVs 2.0 to 2.5 meters: 55- to 65-inch TVs 2.3 to 3.0 meters: 65- to 75-inch TVs 3.0 meters or more: 85-inch or larger TVs These are general guidelines, as comfortable viewing distances may vary depending on viewing habits — such as watching content with subtitles or as a family. Larger screens enhance immersion but may cause eye strain if too large for the space. Samsung offers TVs ranging from 32 to 114 inches to accommodate different spaces and viewing preferences. How Lighting Affects TV Selection Viewing times and lighting conditions vary from home to home, making the viewing environment an important consideration when choosing a TV. In bright spaces, screen brightness and reflection reduction are key, while contrast ratio matters more in darker settings. ▲ Samsung Neo QLED 4K delivers bright, vivid picture quality in well-lit spaces, while Samsung OLED TV offers deep blacks and exceptional contrast in dark environments. For sunlit living rooms, Neo QLED TVs provide high brightness for clear viewing. OLED TVs, meanwhile, deliver exceptional contrast — making them well suited to darker spaces. However, advances in display technology are making lighting conditions less of a constraint. OLED TVs with Glare Free technology minimize reflections, maintaining a clear picture even in brightly lit rooms. 2 AI Gamma technology analyzes scene brightness in real time and automatically adjusts gamma levels based on ambient lighting. It brightens dark scenes to preserve detail in well-lit rooms and reduces glare while enhancing contrast in darker settings. These adjustments help minimize eye strain without compromising picture clarity. How Samsung TV Display Technologies Compare ▲ Each display technology offers a distinct viewing experience, with unique strengths in brightness, contrast, and color expression. Display technologies produce light and color differently, each offering advantages depending on viewing conditions and intended use: OLED: Relies on self-emissive pixels rather than a backlight to deliver near-perfect blacks and fast response times. Mini LED: Employs smaller LEDs than conventional backlights to produce strong contrast, particularly for HDR content. Neo QLED: Combines Quantum Matrix Technology for precise Quantum Mini LED backlight control with Quantum Dot technology that accurately reproduces 2,140 Pantone colors and 110 skin tones. Micro RGB: Features individually controlled, microscopic red, green, and blue (RGB) backlights for a wide color gamut and precise color reproduction. OLED TVs excel at reproducing deep blacks, making them ideal for movies and TV shows in dark rooms. In brighter spaces, TVs with advanced backlight control have an advantage. Mini LED TVs provide strong contrast at an affordable price, while premium Neo QLED TVs combine rich colors from Samsung’s proprietary quantum dot film with powerful AI upscaling. For vivid, accurate colors and lifelike picture quality faithful to the original content, Micro RGB TVs are another option. How Content Shapes TV Choices ▲ Samsung TVs deliver an optimized viewing experience for different types of content, including movies, sports, and games. Different types of content call for different TV features: Movies: High Dynamic Range (HDR) brings out subtle details and colors in both bright and dark scenes, creating greater depth and realism. Live Sports: AI-powered features enhance the viewing experience through real-time picture and sound adjustments. AI Soccer Mode Pro, AI Motion Enhancer, and AI Sound Controller Pro work together to deliver clearer action and more immersive stadium sound. Video Games: High refresh rates ensure smooth motion, while low input lag enables faster responses to player commands. AI Gaming Optimizer automatically adjusts picture and sound settings based on the game genre. Art: Samsung’s Art TV lineup, including The Frame and The Frame Pro, displays renowned artworks when not in use — transforming living spaces into galleries. Customizable bezels, the One Connect Box, and Wireless One Connect create a picture frame-like appearance, while Samsung Art Store provides access to more than 5,000 artworks through a subscription. How AI Makes TVs Smarter ▲ Samsung AI TVs allow users to adjust dialogue and background audio in content to suit their preferences. Unlike conventional TVs, Samsung AI TVs automatically optimize picture and sound while supporting content discovery and information searches. AI Upscaling Pro: Enhances older or lower-resolution content for sharper visuals on high-resolution screens and more immersive sound. AI Soccer Mode Pro: Adjusts picture and sound to recreate the atmosphere of live soccer matches. AI Gaming Optimizer: Recognizes game genres and tailors picture and sound settings accordingly. Vision AI Companion: Connects with AI services to help viewers search for information and discover related content on-screen. When choosing a TV, consumers should look for AI features that match their viewing habits — from automatic picture and sound optimization for sports, movies, and games to on-screen information searches. TV Buying Guide at a Glance Q. What TV size is ideal for a living room? For viewing distances of 2.3 meters or more, a 75-inch or larger TV is recommended. With 4K resolution now widespread, larger screens maintain sharp picture quality even at closer distances. However, sufficient installation space and viewing distance remain important. Q. What TV size is ideal for a bedroom? Bedrooms typically have shorter viewing distances and limited space, making 42- to 50-inch TVs generally suitable. The ideal size depends on the distance from the bed to the screen, as well as the TV’s overall dimensions including the stand and bezel. Q. Should consumers choose a 65- or 75-inch TV? The recommended viewing distance is approximately 2.0 meters for a 65-inch TV and 2.3 meters for a 75-inch model. If possible, compare both sizes from the intended viewing distances before deciding. Q. Can lower-resolution content still look sharp on a 4K TV? Yes. AI Upscaling enhances lower-resolution content to match 4K displays for sharper viewing. Results may vary by model and source material. Q. Do OLED TVs reduce glare? OLED TVs combine exceptional contrast with Glare Free technology to minimize reflections. The 2025 Samsung S95F OLED TV features a low-reflection layer that diffuses external light while preserving contrast and color, even in bright rooms. Q. Should consumers choose QLED or Neo QLED TVs? Neo QLED TVs provide high brightness and precise contrast, while QLED TVs deliver vivid colors at a more affordable price. Both use Quantum Dot technology, but Neo QLED TVs feature smaller Mini LED backlights for more precise backlight control. Q. What is the difference between HDR and non-HDR TVs? HDR TVs reproduce a wider range of brightness and preserve details in highlights and shadows, creating greater depth and realism. Q. Can I use a Samsung Smart TV without a subscription? Yes. Samsung Smart TVs offer features and free content without a paid subscription. Models supporting Samsung TV Plus provide free channels featuring news, entertainment, dramas, and movies. 3 Samsung Art Store allows users to select artworks and the monthly curated Art Store Streams collection for free. A subscription unlocks access to the full collection of more than 5,000 artworks. 4 Q. Which is better for gaming, OLED or Neo QLED TVs? OLED TVs deliver fast response times and near-perfect blacks, while Neo QLED TVs provide high brightness and strong HDR performance. Both offer high refresh rates, low input lag, and Game Modes, making room lighting and preferred game genres important considerations. Q. How can theater-quality sound be achieved with a Samsung TV? Q-Symphony enables compatible Samsung TVs and sound devices to play audio together, delivering optimized surround sound based on room layout and device placement. Recommended viewing distances may vary depending on individual eyesight, preferences, and installation conditions. ︎ UL Solutions has verified Samsung’s “OLED Glare Free” claim based on the Unified Glare Rating (UGR) standard established by the International Commission on Illumination (CIE) and testing standards established by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). ︎ Channel and content availability may vary by country, region, and model and is subject to change without prior notice. ︎ A separate Samsung Art Store subscription is required for full access to the collection. Requires an internet connection and a Samsung Account. ︎

title: Samsung and IOC Back Young Innovators at Africa’s First Olympic Games
text: Samsung Electronics and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) are spotlighting young innovators from Samsung Solve for Tomorrow (SFT) programme at the Youth Olympic Games Dakar 2026, the first Olympic Games to be held in Africa. The innovators are sharing solutions they have developed to address social challenges in their communities. Launched in 2010, Solve for Tomorrow is Samsung’s global corporate social responsibility (CSR) program for young people, helping them use science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) to address challenges in their communities. Through education and mentoring, students learn to identify problems, develop ideas, and build and refine prototypes. The global ambassador initiative gives them opportunities to present their work internationally. The activities in Dakar build on Samsung and the IOC’s collaboration on SFT’s Sport & Tech theme and their joint delivery of the Samsung Solve for Tomorrow Impact Programme. On an Olympic stage where young athletes challenge themselves and grow, the two organizations are giving young innovators an opportunity to present their ideas, learn from others and take the next steps in their development. ▲ Samsung Solve for Tomorrow students pose in front of the booth. “The commitment we made together with the IOC at Milano-Cortina 2026 Olympic Winter Games was a promise to give young people opportunities to discover what they can achieve through technology and sport,” said Eddie Cho, Head of Corporate Citizenship at Samsung Electronics. “In Dakar, that promise starts to take shape. The ambassadors began by tackling problems in their schools and neighborhoods; now they are sharing their solutions with the world. We will continue this collaboration with the IOC to help young people build on what they learn, gain confidence and make a greater difference in their communities.” “The Youth Olympic Games are about much more than competition. They are an opportunity for young people to challenge themselves, learn from one another and experience the Olympic values of friendship, respect and excellence,” said James Macleod, Olympism365 Director, IOC. “Together with Samsung, we are committed to supporting young people take that spirit beyond the field of play and into their everyday lives and communities. title: Samsung Gallery Makes It Easier To Access Photos and Videos Across Galaxy Devices
text: As people capture, store, and revisit memories across multiple devices like mobile phones and tablets, keeping those moments safe and easily accessible has become increasingly important. To help meet this growing need, Samsung Electronics offers a Gallery sync service in collaboration with Google. 1 Samsung Gallery sync with Google storage gives you access to photos and videos across supported Galaxy devices. Getting started is simple. If your Samsung and Google accounts are set up on the device, you can enable sync in Gallery without creating a separate cloud account. You can also move easily between devices while keeping your photos and videos within reach. For example, take photos on your Galaxy phone and view them in Gallery on your tablet. Sign in with the same Samsung and Google accounts and enable sync on each supported device. 2 When setting up a new Galaxy device, sign in with the same Samsung and Google accounts used for Gallery sync on your previous device. Turn on sync to see previews of your photos and videos. 3 If you need an original file, you can select the file you want and download it to your device easily. To help you make room for more memories, Samsung introduces a new feature that lets you free up space on your device. 4 Once photos and videos are synced to Google storage, you can use the “Free up space” feature to remove the original files from the device and free up device storage, while keeping thumbnails visible in Gallery. ▲ “Free up space” feature Gallery sync uses your Google account’s available storage, which is shared with Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Photos. Google accounts include up to 15 GB at no cost. 5 Support has started with select Galaxy devices running One UI 9 and will expand in phases. To set up sync, tap the Cloud icon in Gallery or tap “Get started” on the tip card or go to Gallery Settings, turn on “Sync photos and videos,” and follow the on-screen instructions. ▲ How to set up Samsung Gallery sync with Google storage Frequently Asked Questions Q. What is Samsung Gallery sync with Google storage, and what are its benefits? Samsung Gallery sync stores photos and videos in Google storage linked to your Google account, allowing you to access them across supported Galaxy devices. Each device must use the same Samsung and Google accounts and have sync enabled. On a new Galaxy device, you can view previews without downloading your full synced library first. Q. Do I need a different app or a new account? Samsung Gallery sync works in the Gallery app. With Samsung and Google accounts set up on your device, you do not need a separate cloud account. Q. Which devices and markets support Gallery sync with Google storage? Samsung Gallery sync is available on select Galaxy phones and tablets running One UI 9, with support expanding in phases. Availability varies by market. Q. How do I turn on Gallery sync with Google storage? On a supported Galaxy device, tap the Cloud icon in Samsung Gallery or open Gallery Settings and turn on “Sync photos and videos.” Follow the on-screen instructions. For access on another supported device, sign in with the same Samsung and Google accounts and enable sync there. Q. Do I need to download my whole library onto a new Galaxy device? No. On a supported Galaxy device, sign in with the same Samsung and Google accounts used for Gallery sync on your previous device, then enable sync. You can browse previews of your synced photos and videos while the originals stay in Google storage. Q. How much storage can I use for Samsung Gallery sync? Google accounts include up to 15 GB of free storage, shared by Gallery sync, Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Photos. The amount available for Gallery sync depends on how much storage is already in use. More storage is available through Google One’s paid plans. If you subscribe to Google One, select the account linked to your plan. Q. Do photos and videos in my Google account appear in Samsung Gallery? At launch, Samsung Gallery only shows photos and videos synced through Gallery after you enable Google storage sync. Content stored in Google storage before then does not appear automatically. Q. What happens to photos and videos I synced from Samsung Gallery to OneDrive? Photos and videos synced to OneDrive remain accessible through its app or website. Direct sync between Samsung Gallery and OneDrive ended on September 30, 2026. Q. What happens if I delete a synced photo or video in Samsung Gallery? Deleting a synced item in Samsung Gallery also removes it from the linked Google storage and other connected Galaxy devices signed in with the same Samsung and Google accounts. The service may not be available in some markets due to regional service availability restrictions. The service is available on select devices running One UI 9, with support expanding to additional Galaxy devices in phases. ︎ At launch, cloud photos and videos shown in Samsung Gallery are limited to content synchronized through Gallery after the service is enabled. Photos and videos previously stored in Google storage will remain in the cloud but will not automatically appear in Samsung Gallery. ︎ The new Galaxy device must be signed in with the same Samsung and Google accounts used for Gallery sync on the previous device. When accessing synced content on a new Galaxy device, original photos and videos remain stored in the cloud, with previews displayed on the device. ︎ Feature availability may vary by market and device model. ︎ Google accounts include up to 15 GB of storage at no cost, shared across Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Photos. Available space depends on existing usage. Gallery sync does not add a separate storage allowance. ︎

title: Beyond the Medal: Samsung Helps Young Athletes Explore What Comes Next at Dakar 2026
text: The Youth Olympic Games Dakar 2026 are under way in Senegal from October 31 to November 13, bringing together some 2,700 young athletes across 25 sports for the first Olympic event ever held on the African continent. As a Worldwide Olympic and Paralympic Partner, Samsung Electronics is supporting the Games with Galaxy technology — from Victory Selfie and broadcast integrations to the Samsung Open Station, an experience space inside the Youth Olympic Village. Having supported the Youth Olympic Games since the inaugural edition in Singapore in 2010, Samsung is going beyond technology at Dakar 2026 to support young athletes’ personal growth as well. For the athletes competing at Dakar 2026, reaching the Olympic stage is the result of years of dedication. But some of the most lasting lessons come from what happens along the way — overcoming setbacks, building resilience, discovering what matters beyond results. That is why, on November 3, Samsung hosted “Beyond the Medal: Your Journey Shapes What Comes Next,” a mentoring session at the Samsung Open Station inside the Youth Olympic Village. By bringing in athletes who have walked the Olympic path before them, the session aimed to inspire pride and motivation in the next generation — and to share the spirit of openness at the heart of Samsung’s Olympic partnership. ▲ The mentoring session held at the Samsung Open Station (Copyright: IOC/ Franco Arland) Two IOC Athlete Role Models 1 — Senegalese canoe slalom Olympian Jean-Pierre Bourhis (31) and Ugandan swimmer Jamila Lunkuse (29) — joined New Zealand tennis bronze medalist Marcus Daniell (36) for a conversation with young athletes. ▲ (From left) Jean-Pierre Bourhis (Senegal, Slalom canoe), Jamila Lunkuse (Uganda, Swimming), and Marcus Daniell (New Zealand, Tennis) (Copyright: Getty Images) Moderated by Lefa Makgato , CSR Manager at Samsung Electronics Africa, the session brought the three mentors together with 28 young athletes from 12 countries to share the journeys that shaped them — and offer a guide for exploring where life beyond sport might lead. Open the Way: Finding Your Own Path Makgato opened by asking each mentor where their Olympic journey began. For Bourhis, who represented Senegal at Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020 and is featured in Samsung’s “ Voices of Galaxy: Paddling for the Future ,” the dream took shape in 2008, when Togo’s Benjamin Boukpeti won a bronze medal in kayaking at Beijing 2008. “As a kid, I realized an African paddler could reach the podium,” he said. “Rio 2016 showed me the way could be opened. Now my job is to keep it open for others.” ▲ Jean-Pierre Bourhis (Senegal), IOC Athlete Role Model at Samsung Mentoring Session (Copyright: IOC/ Franco Arland) Lunkuse, who made her Olympic Games debut at 15, recalled that swimming began with friendship rather than ambition. “I wasn’t thinking about medals or the Olympics,” she said. “I just enjoyed being part of something with my friends, and that’s what built my love for the sport.” Daniell, who ended New Zealand’s 109-year wait for an Olympic tennis medal at Tokyo 2020, pointed to choosing tennis over football at 14. “Because I’d given up a sport I loved, I knew I had to fully commit,” he said. Break Your Boundaries: Learning Through Challenges The conversation then turned to the biggest challenges each mentor faced. With almost no whitewater facilities in Senegal, Bourhis had to build his training base in France — while holding down a full-time job as an engineer in electric vehicle repair. “As an engineer, I see a limit as a problem to solve, not a wall,” he said. “I train before work, during lunch, or late at night. What keeps me going is purpose.” Lunkuse spoke openly about the anxiety she faced ahead of Rio 2016. “I became so focused on qualifying times that I no longer enjoyed it,” she said. “It was only when I took time away that I could see what I was going through and what help I needed — and that’s what got me to Rio 2016.” ▲ Jamila Lunkuse (Uganda), IOC Athlete Role Model at Samsung Mentoring Session (Copyright: IOC/ Franco Arland) Daniell described a knee injury in 2022 that kept him out for nearly two years. “What got me through was having something bigger than tennis,” he said. “Everyone fails. Those who last are the ones who learn to pick themselves up when they fall.” Beyond the Game: Turning Experience Into Opportunity Finally, Makgato asked how the lessons of sport carried into what came next. Through nonprofit work, Bourhis is building a canoeing ecosystem in Senegal. “We’re building it step by step — and building canoes locally makes the sport more affordable, creates local jobs, and leaves a lasting legacy,” he said. “I want to give the next generation the tools to build their own way.” Lunkuse, a youth coach and World Aquatics Athletes’ Committee member, urges young athletes to look beyond results. “Results do not define your value,” she said. Similarly, Daniell — an IOC Athletes’ Commission member and founder of High Impact Athletes, a nonprofit connecting athletes with charities — advised: “Look for a goal beyond personal success. For me, that was what kept pushing me forward.” ▲ Marcus Daniell (New Zealand), Tokyo 2020 Olympic Medalist at Samsung Mentoring Session (Copyright: IOC/ Franco Arland) Opening Possibilities for the Next Generation ▲ Lefa Makgato, CSR Manager at Samsung Electronics Africa, moderated the session. (Copyright: IOC/ Franco Arland) Makgato closed the session with a story of her own. Growing up in a small township in South Africa, she first encountered a computer at 18 — at one of Samsung’s Solar Powered Internet Schools. She later joined Samsung Electronics Africa, where she now leads CSR programs across the continent, including Solve for Tomorrow, giving the next generation the kind of opportunity she once received. Having seen firsthand how a single opportunity can change a life, she had good reason to stand before the young athletes that day. “I know firsthand how access to technology and education opens doors you may never have imagined. Where you are today doesn’t determine where you’re going,” she said. “We wanted to encourage young athletes to stay open to new ideas and recognize the potential they have to shape their own futures.” ▲ (From left) Jamila Lunkuse, Jean-Pierre Bourhis, and Marcus Daniell took a selfie at the Samsung Open Station. (Copyright: IOC/ Franco Arland) IOC Athlete Role Models (ARMs) have been part of the Youth Olympic Games since Singapore 2010. Selected by International Federations for each sport, these experienced Olympians stay on site to speak with young athletes and lead workshops on topics such as career management and injury prevention, helping shape the athletes of tomorrow. ︎

As a Worldwide Olympic and Paralympic Partner, Samsung Electronics is supporting the Games with Galaxy technology — from Victory Selfie and broadcast integrations to the Samsung Open Station, an experience space inside the Youth Olympic Village. Having supported the Youth Olympic Games since the inaugural edition in Singapore in 2010, Samsung is going beyond technology at Dakar 2026 to support young athletes’ personal growth as well.

For the athletes competing at Dakar 2026, reaching the Olympic stage is the result of years of dedication. But some of the most lasting lessons come from what happens along the way — overcoming setbacks, building resilience, discovering what matters beyond results.

That is why, on November 3, Samsung hosted “Beyond the Medal: Your Journey Shapes What Comes Next,” a mentoring session at the Samsung Open Station inside the Youth Olympic Village. By bringing in athletes who have walked the Olympic path before them, the session aimed to inspire pride and motivation in the next generation — and to share the spirit of openness at the heart of Samsung’s Olympic partnership.

Two IOC Athlete Role Models1 — Senegalese canoe slalom Olympian Jean-Pierre Bourhis (31) and Ugandan swimmer Jamila Lunkuse (29) — joined New Zealand tennis bronze medalist Marcus Daniell (36) for a conversation with young athletes.

Moderated by Lefa Makgato, CSR Manager at Samsung Electronics Africa, the session brought the three mentors together with 28 young athletes from 12 countries to share the journeys that shaped them — and offer a guide for exploring where life beyond sport might lead.

Open the Way: Finding Your Own Path

Makgato opened by asking each mentor where their Olympic journey began.

For Bourhis, who represented Senegal at Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020 and is featured in Samsung’s “Voices of Galaxy: Paddling for the Future,” the dream took shape in 2008, when Togo’s Benjamin Boukpeti won a bronze medal in kayaking at Beijing 2008.

“As a kid, I realized an African paddler could reach the podium,” he said. “Rio 2016 showed me the way could be opened. Now my job is to keep it open for others.”

Lunkuse, who made her Olympic Games debut at 15, recalled that swimming began with friendship rather than ambition. “I wasn’t thinking about medals or the Olympics,” she said. “I just enjoyed being part of something with my friends, and that’s what built my love for the sport.”

Daniell, who ended New Zealand’s 109-year wait for an Olympic tennis medal at Tokyo 2020, pointed to choosing tennis over football at 14. “Because I’d given up a sport I loved, I knew I had to fully commit,” he said.

Break Your Boundaries: Learning Through Challenges

The conversation then turned to the biggest challenges each mentor faced.

With almost no whitewater facilities in Senegal, Bourhis had to build his training base in France — while holding down a full-time job as an engineer in electric vehicle repair. “As an engineer, I see a limit as a problem to solve, not a wall,” he said. “I train before work, during lunch, or late at night. What keeps me going is purpose.”

Lunkuse spoke openly about the anxiety she faced ahead of Rio 2016. “I became so focused on qualifying times that I no longer enjoyed it,” she said. “It was only when I took time away that I could see what I was going through and what help I needed — and that’s what got me to Rio 2016.”

Daniell described a knee injury in 2022 that kept him out for nearly two years. “What got me through was having something bigger than tennis,” he said. “Everyone fails. Those who last are the ones who learn to pick themselves up when they fall.”

Beyond the Game: Turning Experience Into Opportunity

Finally, Makgato asked how the lessons of sport carried into what came next.

Through nonprofit work, Bourhis is building a canoeing ecosystem in Senegal. “We’re building it step by step — and building canoes locally makes the sport more affordable, creates local jobs, and leaves a lasting legacy,” he said. “I want to give the next generation the tools to build their own way.”

Lunkuse, a youth coach and World Aquatics Athletes’ Committee member, urges young athletes to look beyond results. “Results do not define your value,” she said.

Similarly, Daniell — an IOC Athletes’ Commission member and founder of High Impact Athletes, a nonprofit connecting athletes with charities — advised: “Look for a goal beyond personal success. For me, that was what kept pushing me forward.”

Opening Possibilities for the Next Generation

Makgato closed the session with a story of her own. Growing up in a small township in South Africa, she first encountered a computer at 18 — at one of Samsung’s Solar Powered Internet Schools. She later joined Samsung Electronics Africa, where she now leads CSR programs across the continent, including Solve for Tomorrow, giving the next generation the kind of opportunity she once received. Having seen firsthand how a single opportunity can change a life, she had good reason to stand before the young athletes that day.

“I know firsthand how access to technology and education opens doors you may never have imagined. Where you are today doesn’t determine where you’re going,” she said. “We wanted to encourage young athletes to stay open to new ideas and recognize the potential they have to shape their own futures.”

Selected by International Federations for each sport, these experienced Olympians stay on site to speak with young athletes and lead workshops on topics such as career management and injury prevention, helping shape the athletes of tomorrow. ︎

title: Upgraded Sleep Apnea Feature Now Available on Galaxy Ring Following Regulatory Approvals From US FDA and Korea MFDS
text: Samsung Electronics today announced that its updated Sleep Apnea feature 1 is now available on Galaxy Watch and Ring. 2 Following United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance in July, the updated feature has also received approval from Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS). With this update, Samsung becomes the first company in the world to bring sleep apnea risk detection on a smart ring. The updated Sleep Apnea feature, available through the Samsung Health Monitor app, marks a significant leap forward from its predecessor. The enhanced algorithm analyzes a user’s vitals during sleep in greater depth and now provides insight into the level of breathing disruptions detected — going beyond the previous sleep apnea risk assessment to deliver more comprehensive, meaningful information that helps users better understand their condition, which can lead to productive conversations with healthcare professionals. Most notably, Samsung is extending sleep apnea risk detection to a smart ring for the first time. Galaxy Ring’s comfortable, lightweight design makes it easy to wear through the night and convenient for sleep measurement, encouraging nightly wear. With the feature’s low data requirement, users can gain meaningful insight into their sleep health from as little as two nights of monitoring within a 10-day period. By offering the feature on both Galaxy Watch and Galaxy Ring, Samsung lets users monitor their sleep health in the way that best fits their lifestyle. Samsung’s original Sleep Apnea feature previously received groundbreaking U.S. FDA De Novo authorization in February, 2024 — the first of its kind for a wearable device designed to detect signs of moderate to severe sleep apnea. Building on that clinically validated reliability, the updated feature has now also been approved by Korea’s MFDS last October. Samsung will continue to expand the feature’s availability so more people around the world can detect possible signs of sleep apnea and take proactive steps toward better sleep health. This underscores Samsung’s dedication to accessible preventive care, with sleep health serving as a fundamental pillar. “Samsung has long worked to make sleep health a simple and seamless part of everyday life,” said Jongmin Choi, Head of Health R&D Group, Mobile eXperience (MX) Business, Samsung Electronics. “This approval from Korea’s MFDS, along with our introduction of the world’s first support for a smart ring, reflects our commitment to accessible innovation. We are giving people the tools to help spot possible early signs of sleep apnea and take charge of their wellbeing.” The Sleep Apnea feature is an over-the-counter (OTC) software-only, mobile medical application operating on a compatible Samsung Galaxy Wearable and Phone. This feature is intended to detect signs of moderate to severe sleep apnea in the form of significant breathing disruptions in users 18 years and older, over a two-night monitoring period. It is intended for on-demand use and requires two nights of valid data within a 10-day period. This feature is not intended for users who have previously been diagnosed with sleep apnea. Users should not use this feature to replace traditional methods of diagnosis and treatment by a qualified clinician. ︎ Available on Galaxy Watch 9 running Wear OS 7.0 or higher. Support for Galaxy Watch 7/8 will expand through future software updates. ︎

title: Samsung Electronics Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results
text: Samsung Electronics today reported financial results for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026. The Company posted KRW 195.3 trillion in consolidated revenue, another all-time quarterly high, representing a quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) increase of 14%. Operating profit reached KRW 107.4 trillion, making Samsung Electronics the world’s first tech company to exceed KRW 100 trillion in quarterly operating profit. The Device Solutions (DS) Division posted a QoQ sales increase of 15%, with the Memory Business setting an all-time high for quarterly revenue and operating profit, as semiconductor demand is set to remain robust. The Device eXperience (DX) Division posted a QoQ revenue increase of 8% and recorded an operating loss of KRW 0.8 trillion. DS To Sustain Growth by Proactively Meeting Growing Demand for AI Applications The DS Division posted KRW 147.1 trillion in consolidated revenue and KRW 106.5 trillion in operating profit for the third quarter. The Memory Business achieved another record-breaking quarter by managing its product mix, with a focus on AI products, amid capacity constraints. Strong demand momentum for servers led to higher market prices across all applications. Additionally, the Business experienced continued robust demand, driven by AI applications. It significantly scaled up sales of HBM4 on the back of industry-leading product competitiveness while proactively addressing growing demand for server SSDs. In Q4 2026, the Memory Business expects industry-wide competition for AI leadership to drive continued AI infrastructure investment. Memory demand growth is projected to revolve around new CPU and GPU platform-related products, while surging QLC SSD demand will be linked to the expansion of personal AI agent services. The Memory Business will also maintain a sales strategy focused on AI applications in order to solidify market leadership. Leveraging its industry-leading products and unmatched scale, the Business aims to achieve this by further increasing HBM, server DRAM, and SSD sales, while also increasing the supply of high-speed server DDR5 products and QLC SSDs. In 2027, the Business expects AI infrastructure capital expenditure to reach a historic level as the AI ecosystem expands. Additionally, increasing AI-driven demand will far exceed the industry supply in comparison with 2026. The Business also aims to leverage its superior technology to bolster market leadership and optimize product mix in alignment with market trends and customer needs. It plans to lead the high-end market and sharpen its AI-driven portfolio while building a stable sales base by securing multi-year contracts and ensuring timely readiness of new products tailored to the requirements of AI applications. The System LSI Business achieved revenue growth in Q3 2026, driven by the mass production of systems-on-a-chip (SoCs) and image sensors for new models launched in H2. Additionally, the custom SoC business secured projects by establishing new customer partnerships. In Q4 2026, the Business plans to maintain stable production and sales of flagship SoCs and 200MP image sensors. In 2027, the System LSI Business aims to expand flagship SoC sales and strengthen partnerships with custom SoC customers. It also plans to accelerate sales of flagship high-resolution image sensors and diversify into non-mobile applications. The Foundry Business experienced a notable revenue and earnings improvement on HBM base-die sales growth and expanded advanced-node sales, as well as continued order wins centered on 2nm HPC customers, including major hyperscalers. Looking ahead to Q4 2026, the Foundry Business plans to achieve double-digit revenue growth and continued earnings improvement on new mobile products, mass production ramp-up of 4nm NPUs, and expanded memory product sales. In 2027, the Business will aim for revenue growth led by 4nm and 2nm advanced nodes based on strong AI and HPC demand. It also expects to strengthen its global supply capabilities with the commencement of operations at its new fab in Taylor, Texas. SDC To Build On Growth With Enhanced, Diversified Product Lineup Samsung Display Corporation (SDC) posted KRW 8.0 trillion in consolidated revenue and KRW 1.1 trillion in operating profit for the third quarter. For the small and medium display business, SDC reported improved earnings based on solid demand for high-end mobile products, while the large display business expanded sales volume and revenue on the growth of the gaming monitor market. In Q4 2026, SDC expects a positive effect from year-end peak seasonal demand and new product launches, but it anticipates a limited improvement in earnings due to external factors. During the quarter, the small and medium display business will pursue sales expansion by actively responding to customer demand, while the large display business will focus on improving profitability centered on gaming monitors. In 2027, SDC expects continued market demand weakness amid ongoing uncertainty. For smartphones, the small and medium display business aims to increase the portion of premium products like foldables, and for IT, the business will pursue sales expansion through the ramp-up of the new 8.6G IT line and strengthening of the product lineup. The large display business aims to continue pursuing improved profitability centered on high value-added models. MX To Maintain Mobile Leadership by Capitalizing on the High-Growth Premium Market The MX and Networks Businesses posted a combined KRW 37.7 trillion in consolidated revenue and reported an operating loss of KRW 0.6 trillion for the third quarter. Revenue increased QoQ and year-on-year (YoY), mainly driven by new flagship launches including foldables. Earnings increased QoQ with an improved flagship sales mix, but declined YoY due to cost pressures. In Q4 2026, the MX Business plans to drive year-end peak-season sales growth centered on flagships including the Galaxy S26 series, Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, and Z Fold8, as well as new ecosystem products. It will also seek to mitigate profitability risks through efficiency improvements across all business processes. In 2027, the MX Business aims to maintain its mobile leadership by focusing on three strategic priorities. First, it will improve its product mix, centered on flagships with differentiated experiences by customer segment. Second, it will enhance the desirability and deliver tangible value of products through hardware and form-factor innovation. Third, it will minimize declines in profit with agile market responses and operational efficiency initiatives. In Q3 2026, the Networks Business saw a decline in earnings QoQ and YoY due to lower North American and high-margin software sales. In Q4 2026, the Business aims to secure profitability through revenue growth in North America, Korea, and Japan. In 2027, the Business plans to drive profitable growth by securing new orders amid telco investment headwinds. VD/DA Businesses and Harman To Extend AI-Based Product Innovation The Visual Display (VD) and Digital Appliances (DA) Businesses posted a combined KRW 13.9 trillion in consolidated revenue and reported an operating loss of KRW 0.2 trillion for the third quarter. The VD Business saw revenue decline due to the conclusion of major sporting events, while earnings decreased due to increased costs. In Q4 2026, the Business aims to capture peak season demand through strengthened channel partnerships and differentiated marketing, while expanding sales of premium products in order to offset the impact of rising costs. In 2027, while overall TV demand is expected to remain flat or decline slightly, the Business will focus on securing profitable growth engines by delivering differentiated TV experiences, as well as strengthening the service and platform businesses. Meanwhile, the DA Business’ earnings declined due to higher costs related to raw materials and logistics, despite stronger domestic marketing efforts and growth in the B2B and subscription businesses. In Q4 2026, the Business intends to improve profitability with a higher premium mix, and in 2027, it aims to secure profitability by expanding sales of innovative AI products and growing its high-margin B2B businesses. Harman posted improved earnings on expanded audio and automotive sales, with a boost from non-recurring U.S. tariff refunds. Looking ahead, the Business will seek to maintain stable growth momentum by developing new automotive business and extending audio leadership through portfolio enhancements. Shareholder Return: Q3 Dividend Details and Total Payout The third-quarter cash dividend amounts to KRW 4,601 per common share and KRW 4,601 per preferred share, totaling KRW 30 trillion. Of the estimated KRW 90~110 trillion in total shareholder returns for 2026, and with KRW 35 trillion already planned or completed, the company anticipates the remaining funds to be KRW 55~75 trillion. The return of the remaining funds will include a substantial share repurchase and cancellation program, along with cash dividends. The Company recognizes the growing market interest in the price gap between common and preferred shares, and is committed to actively considering and adjusting the proportion of preferred shares in our share repurchase and cancellation program based on market conditions. The next shareholder return policy, along with the final amount of shareholder returns and the specific execution plans for the remaining funds for 2026, will be finalized at the Board meeting scheduled for late January 2027, with an announcement to follow. Third Quarter 2026 Capital Expenditures In the third quarter, Samsung Electronics’ capital expenditure reached KRW 29 trillion, an increase of KRW 12.2 trillion quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) and KRW 19.8 trillion year-on-year (YoY). Capital expenditure consisted of KRW 27.2 trillion spent in the Device Solutions (DS) Division and KRW 1.1 trillion in Samsung Display Corporation (SDC). The cumulative total for the January-September period is KRW 56.9 trillion, up KRW 24.7 trillion YoY, with KRW 52.8 trillion allocated to the DS Division and KRW 2.4 trillion to SDC. The full-year capital expenditure for 2026 is expected at approximately KRW 84.4 trillion, including KRW 76.8 trillion allocated to the DS Division and KRW 3.9 trillion to SDC. For the DS Division, investments are planned for new fabs and other infrastructure to meet strong AI and HPC demand while ensuring readiness for the mid-to long term. For SDC, investments will focus on upgrades to existing production lines.

title: Samsung Ranks No. 5 in Interbrand’s ‘Best Global Brands 2026’ for Seventh Consecutive Year
text: Samsung Electronics today announced that Interbrand, a global brand consultancy, ranked the company No. 5 on its annual “Best Global Brands” list for the seventh consecutive year, with a brand value of USD 105.2 billion. Samsung is the only company based in Asia to remain in the global top five each year since 2020. title: [Hands-On] Comfort, Convenience, and More: A Day With Galaxy Buds On
text: Earbuds have become an everyday essential for listening to music, taking calls, exercising, and working. With all-day use increasingly common, comfort and awareness of one’s surroundings are now just as important as sound quality. To meet these needs, Samsung Electronics has launched Galaxy Buds On, its first open-ear earbuds. Combining a clip-on design with rich sound and AI-powered features, Galaxy Buds On offers greater freedom and flexibility. Samsung Newsroom put Galaxy Buds On to the test to see how they perform in everyday situations. 🕢 07:30 Comfort and Awareness on Every Run ▲ Galaxy Buds On Galaxy Buds On’s clip-on design rests lightly on the ears for a comfortable fit. Even with vigorous head movements, the earbuds stay securely in place. ▲ Users can adjust the band’s angle to fit their ear shape. ▲ Galaxy Buds On features an ergonomic design with speaker and battery placement optimized through data analysis and simulations involving a wide range of ear shapes. Before a run, users can explore routes while warming up without taking out their smartphones. Saying “Hey Google, let’s talk Live” launches Gemini Live, allowing them to ask for running route recommendations and details such as distances and key features. ▲ Galaxy Buds On offers hands-free access to Gemini Live when paired with a Galaxy AI-enabled smartphone. A tap on the back of an earbud starts music playback, and TwinBoost speaker delivers enhanced bass compared to previous Galaxy Buds models for richer sound. The clip-on design lets users hear passing bicycles and runners approaching from behind while listening to music, helping them stay aware of their surroundings. ▲ Users can run safely and comfortably with Galaxy Buds On. Voice commands offer another way to control music playback without touching the earbuds. Users can say “Next song” or “Previous song” to switch tracks or “Volume up” and “Volume down” to adjust the volume. ▲ Galaxy Buds On offers hands-free access to Gemini Live when paired with a Galaxy AI-enabled smartphone. 🕙 10:00 A Smart, Hands-Free Work Companion Galaxy Buds On also proves useful in shared workspaces, thanks to Audio Leakage Reduction 1 technology that minimizes sound escaping from the earbuds. Later, users can ask Bixby about their tasks and hear the details aloud, eliminating the need to search through saved recordings. ▲ Quick Voice Memo Head Gestures feature comes in handy when users have their hands full. They can nod to answer incoming calls or shake their heads to decline them. Simple head movements also let users check message notifications and dismiss alarms. ▲ Head Gestures 🕡 18:30 Clear Calls, Even on Noisy Commutes Galaxy Buds On remains comfortable even after hours of wear, without putting pressure on the ears. The earbuds also maintain call clarity in noisy environments, such as crowded subway stations. Intelligent Clear Call makes this possible. Three microphones, a bone conduction-based Voice Pickup Unit Sensor, and a machine learning-based solution work together to isolate the user’s voice and reduce background noise. ▲ Galaxy Buds On features Intelligent Clear Call.
